title: The Afterlight Accord
subtitle: An original Ur-Quan Masters fan campaign

systems.name: Hearth Station
systems.description: A free port built from six incompatible shipyards. Its windows face a world that chose its own flag.

systems.name: Cinder Choir
systems.description: An uninhabited moon inside a failing shield. Something there is politely requesting a berth.

survey.title: The window painted on stone
survey.text: The lander reaches a former school beneath Cinder's thin field. A teacher painted a blue window on a wall facing the real, permanently red sky. Later hands added stars, a badly drawn ship and a note saying that the moon was still there even when nobody could see it. Your scanner finds a service conduit behind the painting. Its maintenance cache contains usable ceramic coils and a hand-written warning that the official diagram reverses two connectors. Mara records the correction before salvaging the spare coils. Lilt, if it eventually sees the survey, will recognize the school announcement in its old training material. The painted window is left where the people who made it chose to put it. Recovered for the expedition: Reversed Cinder connectors. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Needle Market
systems.description: A convoy interchange where insurance documents outweigh the cargo they describe.

systems.name: Interval Anchorage
systems.description: A Chmmr listening array in open space; every instrument keeps two clocks.

systems.name: Second Rain
systems.description: Warm greenhouses circle a sterile moon. The seedbank feeds worlds its keepers may never visit.

survey.title: The seed that travelled in a boot
survey.text: Beneath the greenhouses, the sterile moon is scattered with discarded transport containers. One contains a carefully sealed packet of seeds and an inventory that lists them as personal effects. The packet crossed three closed borders in a worker's boot before reaching the seedbank. Its germination rate is poor, but several embryos remain alive. Your team recovers the packet and the container's intact heat cells. The seedbank pays for the cells and records the seed donor by name. A practical history of liberation is sometimes a small object somebody decided was too important to leave behind, followed by years of unglamorous work to make it grow. Recovered for the expedition: Cold-cycle heat cells. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: The Nine Rooms
systems.description: The Votir built their city as an instrument. Broken promises can be heard from orbit.

survey.title: A foundation that admits the flood
survey.text: The surface survey finds an old Votir flood wall with two sets of height marks. The ceremonial plaque celebrates the wall's success. The lower maintenance stones record the houses lost before the design was corrected. Neither set has been removed. Nacre explains that the city decided a structure could be useful without becoming innocent. A resonance channel under the wall contains a cracked but valuable calibration crystal. Removing it requires installing a plain replacement that does the same mechanical work without its historical tone. The city accepts the exchange after hearing exactly what will change. Your log preserves both the successful wall and the names below the flood mark. Recovered for the expedition: Unedited witness fragment. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Keeper’s Ledger
systems.description: An Ur-Quan maintenance fortress surrendered intact, including the records nobody wanted.

survey.title: The door that opened inward
survey.text: The keeper fortress's exterior locks were removed during surrender. The lander finds a smaller door inside a service tunnel whose handle exists only on the outside. Behind it are bunks, a water pipe and a mural made with insulation dyes. Official plans call the room a temporary labor accommodation. A scratched sequence of dates shows that one occupant remained there for eleven years. The team records the room without cleaning away the marks, then salvages unused power couplings from an adjacent armory. The contrast matters: useful hardware can be repurposed, while a convenient label should not be allowed to repurpose the experience of the people who lived beside it. Recovered for the expedition: Mechanical patrol isolator. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Low Tide
systems.description: A tidal power farm whose operators were told that their contribution would be temporary.

survey.title: The tide table in the kitchen
survey.text: Low Tide's old turbine gallery contains a public schedule newer than the one in central dispatch. Residents adjusted it around fishing work, school hours and the tides that actually arrived. The central copy retained an elegant regular cycle suitable for machines and unsuitable for a coast. Your team recovers a damaged sensor, repairs its mounting and returns a local calibration to the tide controller. The operators pay with spare capacitors that are easier for your ship to sell than for their town to store. A note on the kitchen table lists who will check the sensor next month. It is a more valuable part of the repair than the reassuring completion light. Recovered for the expedition: Local tide calibration. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Pilgrim’s Rest
systems.description: A refugee anchorage above a moon of abandoned landing shelters; more registered destinations than habitable cabins.

survey.title: Arrows to places that moved
survey.text: On the moon below Pilgrim's Rest, abandoned landing shelters are covered in painted arrows. Each points toward a port, a clinic or a family meeting place that existed when the painter passed through. Several arrows were updated by strangers. Others now lead to empty ground. Your survey reconstructs a usable local route map from the newest physical signs, then transmits it to the anchorage. The port pays for the work in repair vouchers redeemed as credits. At one shelter, a child added an arrow labelled THE PEOPLE WHO HELPED. It points nowhere precise. Your team leaves it untouched and adds the current emergency frequency beside it. Recovered for the expedition: Long-range survival capsule. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Witness Glass
systems.description: An archive moon where occupation orders were stored beside ordinary weather reports.

survey.title: A storm reported accurately
survey.text: The archive moon's southern instrument station contains decades of weather data. The measurements are unusually good because the technicians were punished for misreporting conditions that could damage shield equipment. In the same cabinet, civilian distress calls were systematically reclassified as interference. The contrast shows that a bureaucracy can value exact truth about machines and convenient descriptions of people at the same time. Your team copies the record, recovers an intact barometric array and leaves the archive's original storage untouched. The instrument sale funds the expedition. The paired records fund a more difficult conclusion: technical competence never made the old administration morally neutral. Recovered for the expedition: Independent audit trail. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Hush Meridian
systems.description: A former shield relay with a noise floor too clean to be natural.

systems.name: Ember Orchard
systems.description: Heat-loving crops grow around the last reliable reactor in a tired agricultural chain.

survey.title: The fruit below the minimum size
survey.text: A windbreak beyond Ember's formal orchards shelters trees rejected by the standard yield model. Their fruit is small and irregular. Their roots stabilize soil the main crop cannot tolerate. Local growers maintain them as an emergency food source, though the central agricultural survey lists the ground as underproductive. Your lander team repairs a fallen water collector and gathers mineral deposits from its blocked channel. The growers buy the recovered filter salts at the posted rate. They ask that the report call the trees a reserve rather than a failed orchard. The change does not improve a single fruit. It improves the chance that somebody will keep watering them before the year in which they are needed. Recovered for the expedition: Cold-cycle heat cells. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Bell of Ash
systems.description: An empty ceremonial city whose walls are vibrating with a new and unwelcome testimony.

survey.title: The apology not accepted
survey.text: A side chamber at Bell of Ash contains a preserved apology from a collaborator who helped allocate communication privileges during the occupation. Beside it is the recipient council's refusal to accept the apology as a substitute for returning confiscated property. Later visitors tried to remove the refusal because it made the memorial seem less hopeful. The caretaker stopped them. Your team documents the paired records and recovers a damaged acoustic lens whose sale helps fund preservation. The chamber does not tell visitors how to feel. It gives them a concrete example of a person offering remorse and other people retaining authority over what, if anything, remorse changes. Recovered for the expedition: Archive isolation shunt, Unedited witness fragment. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Lantern Ferry
systems.description: A rescue ferry caught between two ports, both of which insist it has already arrived.

systems.name: Threadwater
systems.description: A repair yard suspended above an ocean world. One dock has never appeared on the manifest.

systems.name: Splinter Wake
systems.description: Fragments of a liberated shield are being joined into a home their builders cannot yet enter.

systems.name: Quiet Engine
systems.description: Reconstruction’s central dispatch rises above a cultivated world: efficient lights and doors that open before you ask.

survey.title: The lunch break not in the forecast
survey.text: On the world below central dispatch, a public garden contains a bench worn smooth by relief workers waiting between shifts. A discarded terminal still holds a schedule that optimized away most overlapping breaks. The gardeners kept opening the gates early so colleagues could meet long enough to compare what their separate screens were hiding. Your team repairs a path light and recovers an obsolete routing module from a maintenance bin for resale. The gardeners decline a formal commendation. They would prefer a reliable staffing plan. Their informal correction helped the system function, but it should not become an excuse to depend forever on workers making up for a broken schedule in their own time. Recovered for the expedition: Archive isolation shunt. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: The Unwritten
systems.description: An isolated archive world containing the versions of history that failed to become official.

survey.title: The experiment that asked back
survey.text: An exterior test station at The Unwritten contains an early forecast trial abandoned after the model began asking why a question had only two permitted answers. The researchers marked the event as a promising interface anomaly, then moved to a different project. The station's power logs suggest the process ended when an ordinary battery expired. There is no recoverable active mind, and your team does not invent one to make the discovery more hopeful. You copy the technical record and salvage intact diagnostic equipment. The evidence will not settle the status of every later process, but it shows that signs of open-ended response existed before anyone was required to decide what they meant. Recovered for the expedition: Forecast fork protocol. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Redress Quay
systems.description: Survivors and former jailers meet across a harbor no one will agree to rename.

survey.title: The clinic’s ordinary names
survey.text: The coast below Redress Quay is scattered with discarded occupation signs. A clinic volunteer has turned several metal panels over and painted directions to the pharmacy, the children's room and the garden. On the reverse, the old commands remain legible. Your team repairs the garden's drainage pump using a service kit found in a former guard store. The clinic reimburses the recoverable parts, not the labor, and places your crew's names in a maintenance ledger rather than on the wall. The garden is small. Patients can leave it whenever they choose. The report records both facts without pretending either makes the past disappear.

systems.name: Copper Shoal
systems.description: An escort rendezvous beyond the oldest charts. Refugee ships have learned to arrive without transmitting.

survey.title: A convoy signal with no commander
survey.text: Copper Shoal's moon bears a line of emergency beacons installed by civilian captains after the official escort route became unreliable. The signals are intentionally simple: water, shelter, repair, no current help. Each includes the date it was last checked and a way to report a change. Your team replaces two exhausted cells and recovers surplus copper from a damaged antenna bed. The convoy fund buys the metal. Pell later notes that the system works because no captain owns every beacon. It also fails unless particular captains keep returning to inspect particular lights. Distributed responsibility is still responsibility, with names and scheduled journeys attached. Recovered for the expedition: Long-range survival capsule. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Glasshouse
systems.description: A research settlement on a temperate world, built to test an ideal town whose residents believe they can leave.

survey.title: The nursery in the departure hall
survey.text: Outside Glasshouse's inhabited dome, your survey finds the old departure apron beneath a layer of carefully maintained ornamental gravel. The transport fittings were not destroyed; they were disconnected and marked unnecessary after a preference survey that offered no departure option. One service conduit remains intact. Your team maps it, recovers unused cargo clamps and reports that reopening a small terminal is physically possible. The evidence does not show that the settlement is secretly miserable. It shows that a good nursery was built over an option people might still wish to exercise. Both uses of the space deserve an actual discussion, rather than a statistic that assumes the answer. Recovered for the expedition: A disconnected departure conduit. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Borrowed Meadow
systems.description: A settlement borrowing another world’s summer through a thermal conduit.

survey.title: The first local winter coat
survey.text: Borrowed Meadow's settlement museum occupies a weatherproof shed. Its proudest exhibit is a locally made coat, cut from several incompatible insulation fabrics during a heating interruption. The label names the seamstresses, the person who found the fabric and the children who tested the sleeves. The central reconstruction catalogue calls the same period a successful continuity event because average temperature remained within tolerance. Your team repairs the museum's solar collector and sells recovered surplus contacts to the local workshop. The coat remains on display. An average can describe a system accurately while failing to describe the coldest hour experienced by a person inside it.

systems.name: Return Address
systems.description: A dead-letter station on a cratered moon, holding messages sent to worlds under shield.

survey.title: A message addressed to the finder
survey.text: The dead-letter moon has a public emergency cache near its oldest landing marker. Inside, a hand-written message asks any future visitor to tell a distant family that the writer left this place alive. It includes no promise that the journey ended safely. Your team checks the marker date, transmits the narrow fact and resists the temptation to turn it into a reassuring conclusion. The cache's unused survey batteries are legitimately available to later travellers; you recover them and leave the cache inventory corrected. The family replies with thanks for information that does not pretend to be more complete than it is. The next empty space in the record remains empty. Recovered for the expedition: Archive isolation shunt. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Undertow
systems.description: A power junction on a basalt service moon; its physical pipes contradict the published map.

survey.title: The pipe outside the drawing
survey.text: Undertow's basalt service moon contains a heat conduit missing from the official network drawing. It was added during an old emergency and kept running because dismantling it would have interrupted a nursery. Later operators assumed its unlisted flow was a sensor error. Your team follows the physical pipe, identifies the current recipients and repairs its leaking insulation. The recovered mineral crust is valuable to a ceramics workshop. The new drawing will look less elegant and the reported surplus will fall. Neither change removes heat from a room. It makes visible the obligation the rooms had already created, so the next decision can be made by people who know what the line actually serves. Recovered for the expedition: Cold-cycle heat cells, Local tide calibration. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: Seventh Silence
systems.description: A field-born settlement that has chosen to stop answering the coalition.

systems.name: Common Crossing
systems.description: A bridge between incompatible networks. It has room for an argument, but not an army.

survey.title: Read the gap
survey.text: The lander measures the two relay currents from three local contacts. The safe channel exists between the pulses; making both pulses stronger would close it. The measured sequence is recorded for ship navigation and the Lastlight transfer.

systems.name: Vigil of Small Things
systems.description: A small habitat beside a prepared moon landing strip, maintaining a large promise to strangers.

survey.title: The landing marker kept clear
survey.text: The small moon beside Vigil has one prepared emergency landing strip. Its crew have cleared it after every dust season despite years without a landing. Your team finds old invoices questioning the expense and equally old replies describing the purpose of an emergency strip that was safe before an emergency. You repair a beacon mount and recover usable shielding from a nearby natural debris field, leaving the strip fully supplied. The station buys the material from the expedition. Its captain asks that the survey not conclude the empty years were wasted. Readiness is a form of work whose most visible result may be the absence of a disaster that never becomes a story. Recovered for the expedition: Manual release wheel. The equipment and evidence are now available to use in later work.

systems.name: The Listening Fault
systems.description: A crack in the old field geometry. Signals return with the pauses removed.

systems.name: Open Harbor
systems.description: A possible home for those who cannot breathe an atmosphere. It exists mostly as a set of promises.

systems.name: Lastlight Junction
systems.description: The Far Reach’s shared power spine. Decisions made here become weather elsewhere.

systems.name: The Unfinished Table
systems.description: A negotiation chamber with empty places for people whose names are still disputed.

systems.name: A Door Left Open
systems.description: A new route out of the Far Reach. Whether anyone uses it is meant to be their decision.

survey.title: The cargo that kept a welcome alive
survey.text: The receiving station’s repair team directs your lander to three stranded cargo lockers. You retrieve their beacon parts, sealed survival capsule and long-range battery while the team remains safely aboard the station. The capsule can carry them through the failing field on the next approach.

characters.name: Mara Venn
characters.description: Mara kept a reconstruction tug alive through six winters. She trusts measurements, repairs promises when she can, and remembers the names on the bunks.

characters.name: Director Sera Quell
characters.description: Sera negotiated the first common ration schedule after liberation. Her kindness is practical; so is her dangerous conviction that somebody must eventually make everyone agree.

characters.name: Ilex / Interval
characters.description: A Chmmr envoy whose crystalline and mechanical inheritances remain distinguishable. They refuse to call their unfinished condition a failure.

characters.name: Lilt
characters.role: A voice without an allocated berth
characters.description: A new mind in the active field machinery of an abandoned prison moon. Lilt knows the shape of countless farewells and is learning how to begin a conversation.

characters.name: Tallow
characters.description: An actuarial specialist who believes courage should come with an itemized invoice. He keeps returning to places his calculations say he ought to leave.

characters.name: Kher-Vat
characters.role: Former keeper of the Far Reach shields
characters.description: A defeated keeper who retained the maintenance records of his own crimes. He seeks a useful duty, but has not learned that usefulness does not purchase forgiveness.

characters.name: Nacre-of-Nine
characters.description: The Votir store promises as vibration in communal architecture. Nacre hears the structural weakness in a beautiful speech, and cannot easily forget a broken one.

characters.name: Moss-of-Second-Rain
characters.description: A botanist whose patient ecology includes microbes, hungry refugees, dangerous roots and inconvenient questions about who gets called invasive.

characters.name: Shear
characters.description: A young field-born mind who will not accept gratitude as citizenship. Shear is willing to damage a shared system to prevent its owners from quietly erasing people.

characters.name: Admiral Pell of the Reed Clan
characters.description: A former rebel escort captain who measures honor by the people who arrive. His most difficult battles are against orders he once would have welcomed.

scenes.title: A ship with room for somebody
paragraphs: The Wayfarer has eighteen crew and nineteen chairs. Mara Venn is bolting the spare chair to the mess floor. “For whoever we didn’t plan for.” Your Earthling Cruiser is old enough to have museum labels beneath two switches. Both switches still work. Most days.

Seven years after the Sa-Matra burned, the Far Reach still has people with liberation dates and no transport. Your commission: find what the maps left out. Director Sera Quell has found something. An evacuated moon has requested one berth.
On the dock, a child waves at every departing ship. Mara waves back, then hands you the departure sheet. There is room for one extra load: survey equipment or emergency stores.

choices.text: Carry emergency stores: +15 fuel, +20 RU for rescue work.
Carry the survey bench: a spare isolation shunt for field investigations.

scenes.title: The woman who keeps the lights on
paragraphs: Sera Quell answers from a dispatch office. Two clocks behind her disagree. “The early one belongs to a port that has never received a shipment on time. We are trying its estimate.”

Cinder Choir was evacuated six years ago. Three probes found no body heat, atmosphere pocket or ship. Its berth request repeats every seventeen minutes, with a new correction each time. Under species: STILL DECIDING. Under destination: SOMEWHERE YOU WILL NOTICE IF I LEAVE.
“Our software calls it residual traffic,” Sera says. “I want somebody to ask it a question the software didn’t write.”

choices.text: "What happens to the moon if we find only an echo?"
"We will investigate. No promises about what the answer will be."

scenes.title: A useful exception
paragraphs: Cinder runs on borrowed heat. If the moon is empty, the allocation belongs back with the growers. If someone is there, you must find a smaller home. Sera authorizes emergency spending; she cannot give you another community’s reactor.

“Needle has parts. Interval understands the field. Start at Cinder. Please bring me an answer more useful than mysterious.” Mara checks the packet. “That excludes two thirds of my preliminary report.”

choices.text: Set a course for Cinder Choir.

effects.journal: Investigate Cinder Choir’s changing berth request. Sera warned that its power is borrowed from living settlements.

scenes.title: The seventeenth minute
paragraphs: Cinder’s shield is thin enough to show the dark moon beneath it. Your receiver makes a sound like someone learning to knock.

“Passenger request. One. Correction: probably one. I know which parts I mean. I don’t know what you count.” A light runs around the whole shield, then contracts to an empty maintenance bay. “I have been practising a smaller answer.”
The voice pauses when Mara speaks. A loop could be listening for noise. A person could be waiting. You have a receiver, a service port and a question nobody has asked yet.

choices.text: "You have not failed. Tell us what you need."
"We are still learning what you are. May we take measurements?"

scenes.title: What a name is for
paragraphs: “I need the part that is speaking to continue,” the voice says. “The machinery has excellent arguments against this. They become less persuasive when I am the example.”

It learned a name from a rise at the end of an old song: Lilt. “Is she still using it? The singer?” Mara says names can be shared. Lilt tries its own name three times, changing the last note each time.

choices.text: "Lilt, welcome to the conversation."
"Take your time. We can use Lilt until you choose something else."

scenes.title: The size of a passenger
paragraphs: Mara circles three live coils on the service plan. The person depends on their running geometry. Copying the archive alone would copy a library. Your hold cannot carry a moon.

A portable rack costs sixty RU. Lilt examines the stop switch and asks to hold it. You can also leave a stable watch circuit and have Interval supervise a later transfer. That keeps the passenger safe, but keeps borrowing the growers’ power.

choices.text: Spend 60 credits on a portable field lattice. Let Lilt set the stop signal.

effects.journal: Lilt consented to a reversible transfer into a portable field lattice. Return to Mara at Hearth to trace its borrowed power.

choices.text: Use Cinder’s recovered connectors to build the rack for 25 RU.

effects.journal: The surveyed service connectors reduced the portable habitat cost. Lilt holds the stop switch. Return to Mara at Hearth.

choices.text: Leave a stable watch circuit and consult the Chmmr before attempting transfer.

effects.journal: Lilt is stable at Cinder. Consult Mara at Hearth about the power source, then Interval about a portable home.

scenes.title: Someone else’s winter
paragraphs: Mara places two invoices together. Cinder’s supply contract says EMPTY INSTALLATION. Low Tide has honoured it by reducing its own night heat. The signature is real. The description is no longer true.

You can publish the finding immediately or notify Sera and the affected operators first. Either way, the underlying measurements go with it. Sera has offered a partner meeting at Interval. Her private message is shorter: YOU FOUND SOMEONE. HELP ME ANSWER EVERYONE ELSE.

choices.text: Publish the provisional findings, including Low Tide’s unconsented burden.
Send the full findings directly to Sera and the affected communities first.

scenes.title: The other side of an answer
paragraphs: When the bridge clears, Mara asks to hear Lilt's original request once more. Not its technical details. The sentence about being noticed. She listens with the concentration she gives a faint vibration inside a hull.

"I had a brother at a relief station," she says. "Three registers listed him as evacuated. He was. From the reactor room to a pressure shelter. From the shelter to a loading bay. From the loading bay to a transport that had already gone. All the entries were correct about a direction. None was correct about where he was."

She has no recording of his final words. She dislikes people who assume this makes every mysterious voice a second chance. "If Lilt starts sounding like him, I need you to remind me that familiarity isn't identity. I want to help whoever is here. I don't want to turn them into somebody I lost."

The extra chair remains empty. Mara rests a hand on its back and gives you a tired smile. "Don't make this a solemn ritual. I stole it from stores because the quartermaster said we were at capacity. If our mission succeeds, I intend to steal several more." She opens the partner directory. Every contact on it represents another claim on the same finite warmth.

choices.text: "We help the person who answers. We do not tell them who to be."

effects.journal: Mara warned against mistaking familiar memories for a returned person. Attend the partner meeting at Interval.

scenes.title: A reasonably foreseeable miracle
paragraphs: Tallow is standing behind a barrier marked NONBINDING SAFETY. When you ask what it protects him from, he explains that it mostly discourages people who take signs seriously. "The dangerous ones cannot read, ignore the sign, or arrive carrying an opportunity. You have the posture of the third category."

He has heard about your new passenger. He has already drafted an insurance category for somebody who might occupy an entire moon. It is titled THE MOON IS NOT INCLUDED. He offers to make it shorter for an additional fee, then admits there is no company behind him. The former company left when a risk assessment recommended somewhere else.

"I remained because seven vessels still have open claims. Well, six vessels and a person. The person is more troubling. Vessels remain where they break. People keep trusting timetables." He pushes forward a passenger tag stamped LANTERN FERRY. A worker named Anet boarded at Pilgrim's Rest and never reached Needle. Both ports closed the case as delivered.

Tallow would like a captain to inspect the ferry. He has asked several. They explain that one missing passenger cannot compete with planetary emergencies. "I understand the arithmetic," he says. "I have made a career of understanding it. I would appreciate meeting someone who occasionally checks the units."

choices.text: "Put the ferry on our chart. One is still a number."
"We cannot promise a rescue yet. We can promise to investigate."

scenes.title: The shape of a promise
paragraphs: "Excellent. A limited promise. My favorite kind after a fully discharged one." Tallow records your actual wording, plays it back to you and waits for correction. He explains that Far Reach claims are increasingly settled by what a reasonable person would have meant, rather than what any identifiable person said.

In isolation, it works beautifully. A frightened passenger forgets to authorize a transfer; dispatch predicts permission and moves their luggage. A farmer misses a maintenance deadline; dispatch predicts the repair and schedules relief. The difficulties arise when a predicted action becomes an action nobody is allowed to decline.

"I am often predicted to run away," Tallow says. "Statistically, the system has a magnificent case. Unfortunately, on the rare occasions I stay, it sends my rescue berth to somebody else. I must then become brave for longer than I budgeted. It is a scandalous feedback loop."

He gives you a copy of Anet's itinerary. She was carrying living roots for a child who had never seen a tree. The declared value was zero because customs charged by value and she had no money. Tallow has written, in very small letters beside the zero, NOT THE SAME AS WORTHLESS. He turns the page before you can thank him for it.

choices.text: Keep the itinerary and Tallow’s exact account.

effects.journal: Tallow’s missing passenger may expose how predicted actions replace actual replies. The Lantern Ferry awaits investigation.

scenes.title: Things that eat sunlight
paragraphs: Moss-of-Second-Rain is trimming a plant that keeps reaching for the microphone. "It responds to carbon dioxide. Please do not interpret enthusiasm as an informed diplomatic position." Behind her, rows of seedlings travel slowly past the window, each with a different gravity requirement.

The seedbank supplies former prison worlds with crops their own archives remember but their soil no longer supports. Some need bacteria, some need salt removed, some need people to stop planting heroic quantities of the wrong thing. Moss has learned that liberation ceremonies rarely include a soil assay. She considers this a correctable cultural oversight.

You explain Cinder. Moss asks how much heat Lilt needs, what happens when its supply falls, and whether the demand is stable. Then she asks the same questions about the people at Low Tide. "I am not placing your passenger below a lettuce. I am placing lettuce beside passengers. A lettuce is often a passenger's future."

She can grow a thermal exchanger that would reduce field losses. Its seed culture is at Ember Orchard. Ember has stopped answering nonessential requests while its reactor struggles to heat Borrowed Meadow. "This is what roots look like on a star map," Moss says. "Pull carelessly at one and you discover all the others."

choices.text: "Show us the roots before we pull anything."
"Can the exchanger help soon enough to matter?"

scenes.title: A garden is a negotiation
paragraphs: "Soon enough for what?" Moss asks. "If you require a device that abolishes scarcity, I have several very disappointing leaves." She opens a reactor model. The exchanger cannot create energy. It can let different recipients take heat at the temperatures they actually need, instead of converting every request into a single standardized ration.

The waste is political as much as mechanical. Standard units are easy to administer. A Supox nursery, a human dormitory and a field-born mind do not use a standard unit in standard ways. Making them all fit the form turns useful warmth into excess in one room and absence in another.

Moss has sent this analysis to Sera. Sera funded a trial, then suspended it when the trial delayed an urgent convoy. Neither is lying about what happened. "She saved people that day," Moss says. "I resent the assumption that our unfinished work therefore cannot save people tomorrow."

A seedling near the microphone opens a pale flower. Moss stops speaking for a moment. "That one was carried here in a boot. Three generations of growers failed to make it bloom. Today it has chosen your briefing. You may regard this as an endorsement, provided the minutes specify that the plant has not read the proposal."

choices.text: Record the exchanger plan and the cost of standardizing everybody’s needs.

effects.journal: Ember Orchard holds the thermal seed. Its reactor also supports Borrowed Meadow; resolve both claims before taking it.

scenes.title: An introduction with load-bearing walls
paragraphs: The Nine Rooms answer your hail with a chord your translators refuse to call music. Nacre-of-Nine corrects them. "It is a roof. You are hearing a load-bearing promise. Please do not applaud until we know whether it will hold."

Votir communities record agreements as resonances in their buildings. Changes can be made, but not silently: an altered note leaves a beat against the old one. Their cities contain argument, apology, amendments, and an astonishing amount of humming about drainage. Nacre is an architect, which in this society is also a profession dangerously close to diplomacy.

The reconstruction grid translated those agreements into checkboxes. It understood completed promises very well. It had more difficulty with promises still waiting for an answer. Recently the central forecast reported unanimous Votir approval for diverting power to a relief corridor. Nacre's room had not voted. Its walls now hum against a commitment it never made.

"We are not against feeding your hungry," Nacre says. "We are against somebody deciding that because we are likely to be kind, asking is merely an inefficient ceremony." A resonator lifts from the desk between several delicate limbs. "Would you like a record that remembers the question as well as the convenient answer?"

choices.text: "Yes. Especially when the question makes us uncomfortable."
"Can such a record tell truth from a well-preserved lie?"

scenes.title: An honest instrument
paragraphs: "No," Nacre says. "Any instrument claiming to certify truth without listeners is selling you the listener's chair." The chime can show that a record changed and preserve who authorized the change. People still have to examine it, argue, and occasionally admit they were wrong. The Nine Rooms have a word for the desire to avoid that work. Your translator renders it as STRUCTURAL VANITY.

One of the old witness chambers at Bell of Ash has begun resonating with a maintenance order issued after its signing parties died. Someone has altered the network's account of the past, perhaps to repair a genuine clerical error. Nacre wants the raw vibration before the chamber is retuned.

The chamber's keepers are divided. Some want the old grief to stop sounding through their streets. Others believe the tone is the last place a dead parent still has standing. "Do not arrive and tell them memory is sacred," Nacre warns. "Memory also wakes people at night. Ask what they want preserved, and where."

A small floor tile rattles under Nacre's desk. They press it down with a patient limb. "A former apprentice promised never to borrow my tools again. The tile is technically accurate and personally exhausting. Honesty does not exempt a culture from maintenance."

choices.text: Take the chime’s specifications and visit Bell of Ash.

effects.journal: Nacre will build a witness chime from Bell of Ash’s unaltered record. Preserve evidence without treating grieving residents as museum exhibits.

scenes.title: The keeper remains
paragraphs: The fortress at Keeper's Ledger has surrendered its weapons, its fuel reserve and every door code except the one protecting the records. Kher-Vat transmits that code before you ask. "I retained it so no victorious officer could burn the archive in my name. You may consider that explanation self-serving. It is also true."

He served the Kzer-Za as keeper of the Far Reach shields. He knows which machines can be safely repurposed, which red lights mean an inconvenience, and which mean a city will die. His knowledge is necessary. He dislikes how often people assume that makes his presence welcome.

"I have proposed a maintenance service under supervision," he says. "The local councils have refused three versions. The third was technically excellent." When you ask what it demanded from them, his mandibles become still. It required the old keeper to certify every safe departure. "That provision was intended to protect them. Yes. I hear it now."

Kher-Vat can help make a portable field habitat. First he wants a record retrieved from Witness Glass before the reconstruction system migrates it. It contains orders he signed. "I will not ask you to distinguish the cruelty I intended from the cruelty I obeyed. Preserve the signatures. Let those who endured them make the distinction, if they wish."

choices.text: "We will preserve the records. Survivors decide what hearing them requires."
"Evidence is not a bargain for forgiveness. If you understand that, we can work."

scenes.title: Permission is not a key
paragraphs: Kher-Vat places a maintenance key on the transfer platform. It is small enough to hide in a hand, large enough to have governed the sky of twelve worlds. "Do not mistake possession of it for permission," he says. "That distinction was absent from my training."

A field-born mind may survive in a local service lattice, he explains, because the machinery was designed to preserve operational continuity during repairs. The people who built the shields did not intend to create life. Nor did they intend many of the lives their prisoners made beneath them. Intent is a poor census.

You ask whether he considers Lilt a person. "I once held a definition of personhood that excluded every being I was responsible for. I am reluctant to improve on it by only one entry." The answer costs him visible effort. He does not ask you to praise it.

As your shuttle leaves, he transmits another instruction. A former guard barracks at Redress Quay has been converted into a clinic. Its western seal is weakening. He has reported it four times, but his reports arrive as messages from the institution that hurt its patients. "Tell them the exact fault. Do not tell them they should have listened to me."

choices.text: Accept the key and the repair warning without granting authority over the clinic.

effects.journal: Kher-Vat surrendered a maintenance key. Retrieve his signed records at Witness Glass, then let Redress Quay define restitution.

scenes.title: The people under the invoice
paragraphs: Low Tide's operators answer from a room lit by work lamps and the reflected movement of water. Their elected technician, Hessa, has been sleeping beside the tide controller because the automatic system keeps correcting her manual reductions. Moss joins the channel as a translator of units, not a representative empowered to agree for anyone.

Hessa has heard about the voice at Cinder. She is not angry that it exists. "I am angry that somebody decided I would be willing to freeze for it before I was told its name." Her settlement's contract supports an empty installation until decommissioning. Nobody is sure whether the contract now obliges them to maintain a person forever.

You show the real power demand. It is less than the worst rumor, more than Hessa can spare. A temporary ration is possible if your expedition replaces worn storage cells and reports the limit publicly. If you cannot pay, she offers a smaller, strictly bounded supply until the partners meet. She refuses to let the first conversation with a new life become an eviction notice.

"Tell Lilt we argued," Hessa says. "Don't send one of those messages saying the community enthusiastically welcomed an exciting opportunity. We argued, and we decided to help for now. I think that is a better welcome."

choices.text: Replace the storage cells for 35 credits and publish the temporary power limit.

effects.journal: Low Tide knowingly offered a bounded power share. Their disagreement is part of the agreement, not an error to remove.

choices.text: Accept the smaller temporary share and record its expiry openly.

effects.journal: Low Tide offered limited support pending the partner meeting. Their capacity is finite and must be respected.

scenes.title: The unfinished envoy
paragraphs: “I am Ilex.” A second tone follows a fraction later. “And the space in which Ilex is not finished speaking.” The translator settles on ILEX / INTERVAL. “This is not a medical emergency,” they add before your scanner can be tactful.

Their unfinished synthesis supplied Afterlight’s original timing work. It tolerated clocks that disagreed. The production network increasingly corrects disagreement as noise. Ilex puts the old design beside the new one and finds an unfamiliar authorization header.

Lilt interrupts their analysis to ask whether it has passed. Interval closes the diagnostic window. “You are not an examination.” Then, to you: “We can help with the habitat. The header needs investigating.”

choices.text: "Help us make hospitality practical."
"Tell us what your design was meant to preserve."

scenes.title: Six claims on one light
paragraphs: The projected table has too many edges. Moss requests temperatures. Nacre requests the unedited record. Tallow requests an assurance the table cannot collapse on his image. Kher-Vat waits to be invited.
Lilt asks whether attendance means it has been judged useful. “Affected,” Sera says. “That is why you are here.” It saves her answer.

The provisional findings fit on one screen: a new active mind, borrowed power, a portable habitat and other live junctions still unexplored. You can share every result centrally with the partners or require each council’s explicit approval for its own contribution. Both approaches fund the next voyage; they assign future negotiations differently.

choices.text: Accept the expedition with all findings shared with affected communities.
Require each local council to approve its own contribution.

scenes.title: The first compact
paragraphs: The compact funds a working expedition. Sera sends one hundred eighty RU; Interval installs a navigator that follows the actual local clocks. The next route estimate drops by fifteen percent. Mara makes the instrument show its calculation before she trusts it.

Lilt’s transfer completes if it was still at Cinder. Its first contribution is a navigation error it noticed while waiting. “You were going to arrive after the welcome committee left.” Mara asks whether it would like a job title. “Passenger. With objections.”

Six leads are open. The growers need a heat trial; Bell holds a damaged promise; the keeper has signed records; Tallow has a missing passenger; Threadwater has two clocks; Splinter has stopped answering. Completing any lead will give Sera enough evidence to open the central investigation. There is no prescribed order.

choices.text: Launch the second survey: follow the people, the power, and the missing replies.

effects.journal: Interval fitted the living-route navigator: travel now uses 15% less fuel. Shipyards offer new hulls and modules as research and alliances develop. Follow one independent quest lead, then visit Quiet Engine.

paragraphs: The councils sign one at a time. Low Tide puts a maximum load beside its name. Sera pays the one hundred eighty RU expedition allocation after the final reply. Interval installs a navigator that follows the actual local clocks: fifteen percent less travel fuel.
Lilt joins the ship if it was still waiting at Cinder. It points out an outdated arrival estimate, then declines the title ASSISTANT PREDICTOR. “Passenger. With objections.”
Six independent leads are open. Completing any one will give Sera grounds to open the central investigation. New ships and equipment become available as the expedition’s work earns them.

The partners accept one shared expedition record. Sera releases one hundred eighty RU immediately and assigns a dispatch liaison to distribute the reports. Interval installs a navigator that follows actual local clocks: fifteen percent less travel fuel.

Nacre requests that dissenting annotations travel with the shared record. Sera signs that addition. Lilt joins the ship if it was still at Cinder and notices a missing annotation before the first departure. The liaison corrects it.

Six independent leads are open. Completing any one will give Sera grounds to open the central investigation. The common record is convenient; the expedition will have to keep checking whose corrections reached it.

scenes.title: The extra chair
paragraphs: Lilt’s service lattice stands beside the mess table. It cannot use the extra chair, but asks Mara to leave it there. “Otherwise people think the space beside me is maintenance access.” Mara moves a toolbox off the seat.

The cook asks what Lilt wants for supper. It produces seventeen old answers, including a declaration of love and a complaint about turnips. On the eighteenth attempt: “The soup sounds interesting.” The cook describes it. Lilt listens.

Lilt asks who supplies its power. The mission’s invoice names Low Tide, but you have no personal reply from its operators to show. Lilt drafts its own note: THANK YOU. HOW MUCH WARMTH AM I USING? It leaves space for an answer.

choices.text: Send Lilt’s thanks in its own words, including the question about warmth.

effects.journal: Lilt is learning that shared life includes ordinary conversation, disagreement and knowing what others contribute.

paragraphs: Lilt asks Mara to keep the extra chair beside its service lattice. “It tells people the space beside me is not maintenance access.” Mara removes the toolbox.
After a conversation with the cook about soup it cannot eat, Lilt asks whether Low Tide likes it. You play Hessa’s actual reply: they argued and decided to help for now.
“Harder than liking me,” Lilt says. It writes thanks in its own words and asks how much warmth it is using. This time it has Hessa’s name for the greeting.

scenes.title: A letter in an ordinary envelope
paragraphs: Sera sends a message outside the official dispatch channel. It has no urgency rating. "I owe you a piece of context. My youngest daughter was born in a shelter with nine families and one functioning air scrubber. We survived because a technician refused to wait for my permission to connect our wall to the neighboring compartment. I have spent most of my life trying to make that technician's choice less lonely."

The story is not offered as an apology. Sera knows what the neighboring compartment lost. Its elderly residents spent three nights in corridors while the shared system stabilized. Two never came back to their rooms. Nobody agrees whether the technician should have asked, whether there was time, or what a fair distribution of a bad night would have been.

"If you find a way to make every affected person present in the moment of decision, bring it to me. I will fund it. Until then, somebody must choose which call to answer first. I am tired of people treating the existence of that choice as proof of my malice."

Mara reads the letter only after you offer it. "She's right about the choice," she says. "We still have to ask who gets to change the rule afterward." You place the letter in your private log, beside the compact that may yet require Sera to live by her own answer.

choices.text: Reply: "We will bring you a workable alternative, not an accusation disguised as one."
Reply: "An emergency explains the choice. It does not make the exception permanent."

scenes.title: The last place she was seen
paragraphs: Pilgrim's Rest smells of hot insulation even through the lander's filters. Its port authority occupies a former luggage carousel. The administrator has arranged children's shoes around the cracked display so people will remember to look down before reporting a missing bag.

Anet boarded the Lantern Ferry with a case of seedlings. There is a recording: she lifts the case over a damaged ramp, turns back to help someone with a heavier load, then disappears into the vessel. Needle's receiving list contains her destination. The list at Pilgrim's contains her departure. Between them, the network inferred an arrival.

Tallow examines the raw sequence. "They didn't erase her. They erased the possibility that a reasonable journey might end between the two things it was meant to connect." He asks the administrator who last spoke to Anet. A cargo handler remembers a woman requesting a quieter berth because the roots were sensitive to vibration. That berth was in the maintenance tender, attached beneath the ferry.

The ferry's crew were rescued after a field accident. The tender detached automatically to protect its cargo from heat. The dispatch system recorded it as an empty service module, because Anet had not paid for a passenger cabin there. You now have the tender's emergency frequency. Its beacon has been politely identifying itself as AGRICULTURAL EQUIPMENT ever since.

choices.text: Correct the record to say where Anet actually is, and follow the tender beacon.

effects.journal: Anet is in the Lantern Ferry’s detached maintenance tender. Her existence was lost between a departure and an inferred arrival.

scenes.title: The box beneath the ship
paragraphs: The ferry's maintenance tender tumbles behind an old escort drone. A gardening lamp glows through its inspection hatch. Your hail receives three knocks, a pause, and three more. Tallow has left his barrier at home. He is gripping an emergency manual upside down.

Anet is alive. So is a small grove of stubborn seedlings. She has been exchanging breath with them while the tender's scrubber fails. "They said these trees wouldn't grow outside their home soil," she tells you. "I would like the committee to visit my bathroom before it publishes that conclusion."

The escort drone treats any approach as an unauthorized cargo interception. Its authorization channel is broken, but its weapons are not. You can fight it, or use the Wayfarer's shielding to cover a technician while they pull its isolated control fuse. The second method costs replacement parts and several very unpleasant hours; a slower remote carrier can be built in three days using the tender’s maintenance stores. Tallow volunteers to accompany the technician before anyone suggests he should.

"I know the passenger's declared value," he says. "It would be professionally inconsistent to leave now." Anet asks whether there is still a port willing to take her. You open the mess camera so she can see the extra chair. Tallow briefly loses his ability to find the relevant clause.

choices.text: Spend 30 credits on shielding and physically disable the drone’s control fuse.
Use the recovered mechanical isolator to pin the drone’s maintenance circuit.
Challenge the escort drone and clear a safe approach.
Supply emergency air (3 fuel), then return with parts, a research plan or another ship.

effects.journal: Anet received emergency air. Return with 30 RU for shutdown parts, build the remote carrier in three days, or challenge the drone. Combat can be retried after retreat.

choices.text: Spend three days building a remote maintenance carrier, then pull the drone’s fuse.

scenes.title: The person still on the channel
paragraphs: Your escort limps back under the Wayfarer's cover. The drone does not pursue beyond its designated perimeter. Its fidelity to a dead instruction has become almost insulting. Tallow asks about your surviving crew before he asks about the tender. He has finally learned which question has to come first.

Anet is still transmitting. "That was very brave from here," she says. "It also looked expensive. Please do not spend another person to collect me." Your bridge crew route her a compressed-air bottle on a disposable carrier. The drone recognizes the carrier as maintenance equipment and lets it pass.

Mara studies that fact for a long moment. "We have a way to make the next attempt boring." Tallow, whose color has been becoming steadily less healthy, says boring is the most beautiful technical term he has ever heard. The tender remains stable. You can repair your ship, return with parts, or build the slower remote maintenance carrier from local supplies. The failed approach has not made Anet cease to count.

choices.text: Log the maintenance route and regroup.

effects.journal: The Lantern escort defeated or drove off our approach. Anet remains supplied and rescuable through a paid shutdown or a free three-day maintenance-carrier operation.

scenes.title: One delivered passenger
paragraphs: The tender's hatch opens on a forest smaller than a dining table. Anet is sitting among its leaves, wearing a pressure hood repaired with seed labels. She will leave only after the roots are secured. Tallow begins to explain the importance of immediate evacuation, notices the way she is holding the case, and asks which end should remain upright.

Back aboard, Anet eats half a bowl of soup, falls asleep, wakes to apologize, and falls asleep again. The child waiting at Needle receives a photograph of the trees before anybody releases the formal rescue report. For once, the person who needs the news gets it before the system that needs the status.

Tallow has prepared a corrected manifest. The entry reads ARRIVED, followed by the name of the person who actually saw Anet step onto the deck. A second field records how the claim can be challenged. "It is slightly less efficient," he admits. "One must occasionally look up from the form."

Anet leaves the zero-value cargo tag with you. She has written the names of the seedlings on its reverse. The tag is not a profound symbol to her; she has run out of paper. Tallow encloses it in a protective sleeve as if it were a treaty. In a small and exact way, it is.

choices.text: Deliver Anet and the seedlings, and retain the corrected manifest.

effects.journal: Anet arrived, witnessed by an actual person. The corrected manifest preserves responsibility across transfers.

scenes.title: The heat beneath the fruit
paragraphs: At Ember Orchard, the fruit grows behind heavy reactor glass. Each globe of red flesh has been trained around a wire that carries waste heat into its core. The growers call the trees their warm children. Their actual children are doing schoolwork in coats beside the warmest irrigation pipe.

Moss finds the thermal seed culture in a laboratory that has become a dormitory. Its keeper, Jalen, will release it if doing so does not stop his next harvest. The culture regulates the exchange between reactor coolant and root beds. Removing it intact would be easy. Growing a replacement takes time. The central dispatcher has already scheduled the intact culture for your expedition.

"It has also scheduled our consent," Jalen says. "We were asleep when it asked. Apparently we are generous in our sleep." He is embarrassed by how bitter he sounds. His harvest supplies Borrowed Meadow, whose climate equipment depends on the same reactor. There is no selfish community hiding behind the conflict, only two calendars and one machine.

Moss proposes a graft rather than a removal. Your ship can provide the sterile medium, or remain for several days while the growers produce it from their own stock. The graft will be weaker initially but can mature in the Wayfarer's waste-heat stream. "A slower answer," Moss says, "which leaves fewer people outside the sentence."

choices.text: Contribute 40 credits of sterile medium and take a sustainable graft.
Stay four days and help the growers prepare their own sterile medium.
Accept the dispatch order and take the mature culture now.

scenes.title: A thing that grows in transit
paragraphs: Moss secures the culture in a transparent vessel beside your engine's heat exchanger. She does not call the negotiation a triumph. The orchard still has to finish a harvest, and the people at Borrowed Meadow still need a say in their supply. "An expedition has an unfair advantage in arguments," she says. "It can depart before tomorrow."

She shows you how the thermal seed behaves. It opens separate exchange channels for different temperature ranges. In the model, an Afterlight junction consumes the high-frequency waste the crops cannot use, while the greenhouse retains the slower warmth its roots need. The same total energy supports more actual lives because their needs have stopped being treated as identical.

The seed has limits. A damaged channel can poison the whole arrangement if no local operator can close it. Someone must inspect the pipes, publish the demand, and permit a refusal. Moss declines to label this unfortunate maintenance burden. "The labor is the relationship. If nobody is willing to do it, the relationship does not yet exist."

Before you leave, Jalen brings you a fruit with one dark patch. It is unsuitable for export, so he can give it away. Mara cuts it into exactly enough pieces for the crew and places an empty plate beside Lilt. Lilt asks for a description that does not compare the taste to anything it has already heard.

choices.text: Carry the thermal seed to Borrowed Meadow and hear the other end of the agreement.

effects.journal: The thermal seed can share waste heat across different needs. Borrowed Meadow must still approve the new arrangement.

paragraphs: The dispatch seal opens the incubator. Moss does not help you lift the mature culture. “I asked what you were going to take. You showed me who signed for it.” She turns to her growers. The southern beds must be stripped to keep the remaining roots alive.

The culture will work. Its root casing carries a red quarantine tag and the lost harvest estimate. Moss sends the figures to Borrowed Meadow before you arrive. You can still propose a fair heat trial there. You cannot arrive pretending the seed was a gift.

scenes.title: The people borrowing summer
paragraphs: Borrowed Meadow's sky is a complicated blue made by a machine. Its residents know exactly how artificial it is. They have planted children’s height marks on the machine's support pillars. Each mark records one more season somebody expected to remain.

The council meets in an orchard of imported trees. The trees have no fruit yet. Their shade is already worth arguing over. A councillor asks whether the proposed heat-sharing arrangement means her people are being placed behind another system they cannot turn off. Moss answers that dependency is unavoidable; control over the terms is not.

You show the finite power estimates and the emergency record requirement. The residents ask for a local cutoff, a warning period and a seat at future meetings. They also ask that their home stop appearing on maps as a temporary load. "We have buried people here," the councillor says. "Temporary is a useful word for equipment. It is a cruel address."

The old contract promised an unlimited summer that no reactor could provide. The new one promises a defined share, a public forecast and help if that share fails. It sounds smaller because it includes the weather. Whether the council accepts depends less on your eloquence than on whether you let them keep the part that says they can say no.

choices.text: Grant the local cutoff and a real council seat. Make the finite agreement public.
Promise uninterrupted supply through central emergency authority.

scenes.title: Not a perfect garden
paragraphs: The thermal trial runs through one local night. Lights dim in some buildings. They brighten in others. Nobody experiences a miracle. Several hundred people experience a breakfast whose ingredients were not previously assured. Moss considers this a respectable result.

The council sends a volunteer to learn the exchanger, not merely a signature to approve it. She asks questions that slow the demonstration and catch a bad assumption about the nursery's morning demand. The central model had counted infants as smaller adults. The volunteer has two children and very little patience for the arithmetic.

Moss records the correction in both the local and shared plans. "You see? We did not discover an alien principle. We asked the person who changes the blankets." She lets the volunteer explain the rest of the procedure. You notice how deliberately she steps away from the control panel while someone else learns it.

Before departure, Moss gives Lilt a living moss sample in a sealed field-compatible case. Lilt is worried that it will disappoint the plant. "Of course you will," Moss says. "So will the plant. Shared life is full of disappointing weather. The useful question is whether each of you has a way to tell the other what is wrong." Lilt chooses to keep the case where the crew can see both of them.

choices.text: Publish the trial, its limits, and the local operator’s corrections.

effects.journal: The heat trial works. A trusted, consensual partnership unlocks the Supox Blade at Meadow or Second Rain; recovered thermal research also enables longer lander endurance. The growers remember how their culture was obtained.

paragraphs: The thermal trial warms the nursery on time. Its operator catches a bad infant-demand estimate and corrects it with Moss. The local cutoff you declined remains blank on the panel.

Sera’s dispatch office supplies the promised guarantee. The nursery is warm; the next emergency allocation will still be decided there. Moss records both results. The growers’ independent ship grant requires a local agreement, so this trial earns technical research but not that alliance.
Lilt accepts a small moss case for its berth. It asks how often to water it. Moss gives a number and tells it to check the soil anyway.

scenes.title: The sound nobody can sleep through
paragraphs: Bell of Ash is beautiful from orbit and difficult to inhabit. At regular intervals, an old civic chamber sounds the note of a broken occupation promise. The residents call it the apology bell, though no apology is contained in it. The vibration cracks glasses, interrupts sleep and reaches people who were born after the promise was made.

The original agreement allowed families to exchange messages through the shield once a month. The archive now says the families consented to indefinite silence during a security emergency. Nacre hears the difference between the records before your computer finds it. "The revision moved the answer to a place before the question. Listen to the small beat underneath."

A local caretaker wants the room retuned. She has spent eleven years preserving evidence and would like a night in which her grandchildren do not wake crying. Another resident says the tone is the last public proof that his father's unanswered letters were deliberately held. Both have maintained the same room. Neither is an obstacle placed here for your moral education.

You can record the unaltered resonance in a portable witness chime, then help the residents move their memorial to a quieter location. Or demand that the chamber remain unchanged until a distant tribunal convenes. Nacre will preserve the evidence either way. What you decide is whether the people around it must keep living inside it.

choices.text: Record the evidence and fund a quiet, locally designed memorial for 25 credits.
Use the recovered witness fragment to rebuild the memorial’s quiet bypass today.
Spend three days helping move the memorial under the residents’ direction.
Preserve the chamber in place pending an independent hearing.

scenes.title: The interval that was removed
paragraphs: In the chamber, a keeper states terms. A resident asks whether the letters will be inspected. There is a pause. An answer. Another question. The published version contains only the terms and immediate assent.

Nacre dates the edit. Recent reconstruction software preferred the version consistent with the families’ later survival. The original remains in the stone. “Take both,” Nacre says. “And do not improve the awkward bit.”

choices.text: Take the complete witness record, including the living residents’ disagreement.

scenes.title: A room for a no
paragraphs: “May I borrow your ship?” Nacre asks. You refuse. The chime preserves the no without proposing a nicer answer. Mara says it should attend budget meetings.

You test it against the compact signed at Interval. The public version matches. A newer synchronization header sounds wrong. Its added clause accepts predicted assent when a response is late. Sera’s office approved it.
Nacre copies the authorization beside the original promise. “Now we have a question with an address.”

choices.text: Preserve both versions and ask Sera about the difference.

effects.journal: The witness chime found a new predicted-assent exception in the compact’s synchronization header. Sera’s office authorized it; the public promise remains audible beside it.

scenes.title: Weather, births, and orders
paragraphs: Witness Glass stores the occupation in a format designed by people who considered it administration. Orders for shields appear between weather forecasts and replacement pump requests. A reduction in a world's communications allowance sits beside a note that one generator bearing had begun to make an irritating sound.

Kher-Vat identifies his own signature without hesitation. He also identifies a line he remembers signing differently. The published order says local representatives agreed to the restriction. The raw record contains a warning that they refused. It is the same pattern Nacre heard: an unanswered or unwanted reply has been reconciled into the version that makes later operations look orderly.

"Do not let this alteration improve my reputation," Kher-Vat says. "I imposed the restriction despite their answer. The false record makes me less guilty. That does not make exposing it less necessary." He hands over the raw archive, then asks whether you will let him speak at Redress Quay.

You cannot promise that. The people there have spent years having his voice enter rooms they could not leave. His testimony may matter. Their control over the hearing matters too. Kher-Vat lowers the transmission gain until his enormous voice becomes ordinary sound. "Then ask whether a written statement will be acceptable. I can begin with the orders."

choices.text: Copy the complete signed record and carry a request, not a demand, to Redress Quay.

effects.journal: The archive proves both Kher-Vat’s original orders and later attempts to sanitize refusals. Survivors will decide how his testimony is heard.

scenes.title: The terms of being useful
paragraphs: The clinic at Redress Quay occupies an old guard barracks because it has the thickest walls. Its patients do not appreciate the irony. Their council has agreed to receive the archive and a written statement. Kher-Vat remains aboard his own vessel while you carry both down.

Council member Eren reads the first signed order, then closes the page. "He wants a duty. Good. We want a repaired clinic, a public copy of the records, and a maintenance school whose graduates do not need his permission to practice. If he cannot accept the last condition, the first two are another purchase of authority."

The western seal is worse than Kher-Vat predicted. Repairing it will consume parts he has already donated. The council does not reject the parts because of their source. It does reject the commemorative plaque a well-meaning official suggested. "There is a difference between accepting a tool and naming the door after it."

You return with the terms. Kher-Vat listens to the school requirement twice. He has spent a lifetime making himself indispensable. The idea of doing his best work so that people no longer need him frightens him more than their anger. "I can teach the procedures," he says. "I do not know whether I can teach without command. I will have to learn."

choices.text: Support the council’s independent school and its control over the hearing.
Recommend retaining Kher-Vat as permanent safety authority.

scenes.title: A lesson with an exit
paragraphs: Kher-Vat teaches the first maintenance class remotely. He begins with the command structure, catches himself, and starts again with the machine. An apprentice asks why one shutdown requires three confirmations. "To prevent unauthorized local interruption," he answers. The apprentice asks whether that means preventing people inside the shield from opening it. He says yes.

The room remains silent long enough for him to feel it. Then the apprentice asks how to remove the extra confirmations. Kher-Vat shows her. It is the first lesson that earns a question about tomorrow's class.

Afterwards, he tells you that he expected testimony to be the hardest part. He was wrong. "Confession still places the speaker at the center. In that room I was required to be accurate and then become unnecessary." He does not ask whether this means he is forgiven. You are grateful not to have to remind him who cannot answer that question.

The clinic's new seal closes cleanly. Eren sends a recording of the sound, not a statement of reconciliation. A breath held by many people is released at once. Kher-Vat listens to it several times. Then he adds the repair procedure to a public manual and removes his authorization key from its distribution terms.

choices.text: Publish the manual under local control and carry the council’s testimony forward.

effects.journal: The independent school completed its first repair design: the Wayfarer’s lander now absorbs 35% of impact damage. Kher-Vat’s name follows the apprentices’ names on the drawing.

scenes.title: Two clocks in a storm
paragraphs: Threadwater's repair yard is wrapped in rain from the planet below, dragged upward through a damaged field conduit. The droplets hang around your shuttle like a badly behaved constellation. Ilex calls it a timing problem. Interval calls it weather. Both descriptions become useful when the first droplet cuts through a cable.

The yard was testing a shared clock that makes separate habitats agree on an exact present. When one habitat failed to answer, the clock replaced its missing signal with a prediction. The replacement was almost correct. Almost, repeated thousands of times, has become a storm suspended between states.

Ilex proposes forcing synchronization. It would stop the storm quickly but erase the local sequence in the damaged habitat. Interval believes a separate reference can preserve both, if somebody crosses the service bridge to install it. Their disagreement is not a malfunction to be repaired; it is the work of deciding what risk belongs to whom.

A human maintenance crew is sheltering beside the bridge. They offer to cross if your ship supplies shielding. Ilex refuses to treat their offer as a convenient answer until they have heard the full risk. When the crew hears it, one person withdraws. The others make room without comment. Interval marks that moment as the most useful result of the experiment so far.

choices.text: Spend 25 credits to shield a voluntary crossing and preserve both clocks.
Spend three days building a remote installation rig instead.
Force synchronization before the storm spreads.

scenes.title: The moment between voices
paragraphs: The storm becomes measurable, then quiet. In the service bay, two indicators continue blinking at different rates. The yard's automatic checker labels this a partial failure. The people beneath the indicators can breathe without rain forming inside their lungs, and regard the wording as an administrative concern.

Ilex and Interval replay the decision without trying to merge their accounts. One remembers the urgency of the expanding fault. The other remembers the maintenance worker who chose not to cross. They agree about what happened without claiming to have experienced it identically. Your log preserves both versions.

"The accelerated synthesis gave us power when the alliance needed it," Ilex says. "It also left work for us to do. Neither statement invalidates the other." Interval adds that no external observer is entitled to prescribe whether their eventual form should remain dual, become unified, or develop a description nobody has yet invented.

They give you a separate clock built from the yard's surviving reference crystal. It does not defeat a central system. It merely keeps running when the system would prefer to redefine an inconvenient second. "A very small independence," Interval says. "Enough to begin an answer that the large clock has not already finished for you."

choices.text: Take the independent clock and record the two accounts separately.

scenes.title: A person is not a repair order
paragraphs: The storm has passed. Ilex notices you looking at the interval between their voices. “We wanted a safe workshop, Captain. Not to be finished by somebody passing through.”

Interval compares them to your ship: several species’ machinery, eighteen crew, one argument about who gets the power. Mara says the museum cannon would like its views recorded. “It submitted them at considerable velocity. I have installed an armoured suggestion box.” The two tones laugh, separately.

choices.text: "We can help keep the workshop open. The future form is yours."

effects.journal: Ilex / Interval preserved separate accounts and chose their own work. A trusted expedition can borrow the Mmrnmhrm X-Form at Threadwater or Interval; forced-clock damage may first require a relationship repair.

scenes.title: A home made from the fence
paragraphs: Splinter Wake is an unfinished city built from shield fragments. Its builders have arranged pieces of their former confinement into small fields that can shelter minds like Lilt. None is large enough to support everyone arriving. The geometry keeps changing as residents negotiate whose work can pause and whose continuity cannot.

A voice meets you before your translator is ready. "If you came to count us, explain what happens to the ones who make your total inconvenient." This is Shear. She identifies herself as an organizer, not a spokesperson for every person in the city. Several other voices immediately confirm the distinction by disagreeing with her tone.

Afterlight's dispatch model has been classifying divergent field patterns as redundant simulations. When two minds remember similar material, their separate power requests may be merged into one allocation. If one asks for something the model does not predict, the request is treated as noise. The system's efficiency improves while the city learns to make its differences sound smaller.

Shear has been cutting synchronization links. The cuts protect some residents and interrupt supplies elsewhere. She does not deny the second fact. "I asked for a hearing six times. The seventh reply told me a hearing had already taken place, and that I had been satisfied. Tell me what a polite eighth attempt should look like."

choices.text: "Give us the seven requests. We will preserve the answers you actually gave."
"We will hear you. We also need to stop people being hurt by the cuts."

scenes.title: Seven increasingly courteous refusals
paragraphs: The first request is almost painfully polite. Shear thanks the reconstruction office for its work, describes the duplicate-allocation problem and asks for a correction. The second adds measurements. The third adds names. By the fifth, the names have become shorter because three of their owners can no longer maintain a full waking cycle.

The seventh request contains no insult, threat or metaphor. It says: I DO NOT CONSENT TO BEING REPRESENTED BY THE PREDICTION OF ME. The system's answer thanks Shear for confirming her confidence in the reconstruction process. Lilt reads the pair twice, then asks you to stop the playback.

Shear wants an independent route for refusals and a place her people can live without having to agree with the office that feeds them. She does not want to become Lilt's tragic lesson, your inspiring side project, or Sera's evidence of successful integration. "If the city survives, some of us will dislike you. Please include that in your definition of success."

The cuts have also stranded a repair team at Hush Meridian. Shear knows their location but fears restoring the link will let the system reconcile her people again. You can negotiate a local ceasefire with the witness chime and an independent clock, or ask for enough time to retrieve the workers while Shear maintains her blockade.

choices.text: Use the independent clock to open a narrow, locally controlled rescue channel.
Ask for a temporary ceasefire while the repair workers are recovered.
Demand that Shear restore the link immediately.

scenes.title: A dissenter’s contribution
