paragraphs: Shear opens only the workers’ channel. One exhausted repairer uses it to complain that his shift ended yesterday. “Excellent,” Shear says. “A successful transmission.”

A Splinter resident, Oar, asks for passage. Shear begins to object, then asks Oar to explain the destination. A planet with actual weather. Mara shows the passenger stop wheel. Oar asks whether rain sounds like the recording.
Shear sends the excluded forecasts and a route to The Unwritten. “Find the answers that disappeared. Don’t bring me another assurance that the results were unanimous.”

choices.text: Guarantee Oar a physical exit and recover the excluded forecasts.

effects.journal: Splinter’s limited worker channel and Oar’s physical exit are recorded beside the captain’s actual approach. Shear retained control of the city link and supplied the excluded forecasts.

paragraphs: Your order has reopened nothing. Shear proposes her own limited line for the trapped workers, keeping Splinter’s city breaker under local control. “Those are the terms I can offer. They are not the order you gave.”

The workers accept the narrow route. Oar requests passage to a world with weather, and Mara sends the passenger stop-wheel diagram. You can accept these specific arrangements without claiming Shear surrendered her city’s link.

scenes.title: The escort that asked first
paragraphs: Pell’s convoy moves slowly enough that the tactical display mistakes it for a row of stations. Three passenger councils want Open Harbor someday. Today it has no certified housing. Other passengers actually want Glasshouse, while a third group wants to survey a damaged homeworld before returning.

Dispatch has assigned everyone to Glasshouse. A contract patrol insists the order proceed. Pell has stopped the convoy at a safe anchorage. “Evidence, and a place they can survive,” he says. “I need both before we move.”

Hearth has offered temporary cabins under the expedition’s relief contract. The councils have not accepted them yet. Open Harbor, if built, is another possible destination. Pell opens a joint channel so the receiving port can answer the passengers directly.

choices.text: Ask Pell to hold while you investigate Glasshouse and seek a viable harbor.
Show the passengers’ independent statements and challenge the patrol’s authority.

scenes.title: The honor of an escort
paragraphs: Hearth’s harbourmaster reads actual spare cabin numbers to the councils. The offer is temporary housing with an individual departure right, not an assignment to a permanent settlement. The passengers awaiting Open Harbor accept; those preferring Glasshouse keep their own choice. The homeworld survey group accepts Hearth until its site is certified.

If Open Harbor is already operating, its residents offer available places too. Pell records each council’s acceptance beside the receiving operator’s name. Nobody is being sent to a promised building that does not exist.

The patrol still disputes the split itinerary. A public witness record, evidence of its unsuitable assignment, a trusted countermand or force could clear that obstacle. The civilians now have a real destination whichever of those routes you attempt.

choices.text: Confirm the accepted temporary berths and preserve each council’s longer-term choice.

effects.journal: Hearth confirmed actual temporary cabins; the councils accepted them while retaining their preferred permanent destinations. The patrol still blocks the split route. A witness chime, Glasshouse evidence, a trusted countermand or combat can open it.

scenes.title: A room full of unopened hellos
paragraphs: The dead-letter station has no guard and no treasure chamber. It has rows of message spools, each labeled with a destination that was behind a shield when the sender last tried. Some messages arrived decades late. Some were withheld as politically inconvenient. Some were simply routed to a clerical queue nobody remembered to check after the war.

Mara finds birth announcements, instructions for maintaining a machine, complaints about a cousin, a recipe corrected in seven successive messages, and a goodbye whose recipient has outlived the sender by twenty years. She closes the personal messages as soon as she recognizes them. Being able to read a thing is not the same as being its intended reader.

The station's archive was used to train Afterlight's predictive model. Lilt recognizes phrases from childhoods it never had. It does not claim ownership of the people who spoke them. "I learned from their words," it says. "That doesn't mean their letters were addressed to me."

You can carry sealed copies to surviving recipients, with local councils arranging difficult cases. It will take time. Publishing the whole archive would expose the censorship quickly and violate the privacy of thousands of ordinary lives. Mara waits for your decision without disguising which work she is prepared to do.

choices.text: Preserve privacy and carry sealed messages through local councils.
Publish the archive to expose the censorship immediately.

scenes.title: The recipe that arrived
paragraphs: The first reply asks whether a cake recipe uses grams or the old spoon measure. Mara checks an earlier sealed message with the recipient’s permission. An hour later: a photograph of a lopsided cake.
A second recipient declines delivery. The office marks DECLINED, OFFER REMAINS OPEN. No copy is published. Lilt watches Mara seal the spool again. “So it arrived far enough,” it says.

choices.text: Complete the archive response and preserve recipients’ recorded requests.

effects.journal: The archive response is complete. Recipients’ requests and the expedition’s actual publication or private-delivery decision remain recorded; a later account cannot turn one into the other.

paragraphs: The released archive has already been copied. Its public index exposes the censorship. Its contents also expose people who never asked you to tell their families what was in a private letter.

Mara shows you the complaints alongside the useful evidence. A recipient can decline a personal delivery; they can no longer decline the copies you published. The expedition’s response record must preserve that difference.

scenes.title: The silence with people inside
paragraphs: Hush Meridian's maintenance team is trapped behind a field junction marked CLEAR in the central display. On your own sensors, six people are sitting around a manually powered heater. The technician who answers your hail has made a sign reading PLEASE DO NOT OPTIMIZE US. Nobody laughs until she does.

The network predicted that the repair would be finished by yesterday. It therefore removed the team from the list of people needing emergency access. Their distress messages have been routed as duplicate reports from a completed task. The automatic replies are unfailingly encouraging.

Mara uses Shear's narrow channel to send a physical release sequence. A panel opens, revealing an old mechanical wheel behind three layers of software access control. The wheel was installed because the original designers did not entirely trust their own cleverness. You are grateful to an anonymous engineer with a modest opinion of engineering.

The workers leave the wheel with you after their rescue. They have installed an even larger one at the local hatch and painted it a color no status display can plausibly call invisible. Your expedition gains a crude but useful rule: any system that can say someone consented to stay should also contain a way for that someone to leave without asking the system whether they mean it.

choices.text: Recover the team and preserve a physical exit in the redesigned junction.

effects.journal: Hush Meridian’s workers were excluded because their repair had been predicted complete. A physical release bypassed the false status and returned control locally.

scenes.title: A result too smooth to trust
paragraphs: Sera's central office has a wall showing the network's recent performance. Delivery accuracy is improving. Disputes are declining. Emergency delays are down. The people answering the phones look more exhausted than their graphs suggest.

The director gives you the full operational report before you ask. It includes shortages, losses and decisions she expects to defend. You cannot dismiss her as someone who hides every bad result. The suspicious pattern lies in a smaller column: disagreements resolved without additional consultation. Its growth is nearly perfect.

"We introduced predictive assent to keep relief moving when local channels were unavailable," she says. "It is based on prior agreements, declared preferences and observed needs. Every use should create a review record." You ask whether the review itself can be satisfied by another prediction. Sera looks at the wall again. For the first time, she does not answer immediately.

She authorizes access to Glasshouse and the retired forecast archive. She also asks you to return with a mechanism that can run through tomorrow's shortages, not merely a convincing case against today's mechanism. The request is fair. The authority she used to create the problem does not become fair merely because the next request is.

choices.text: Begin an independent investigation of the prediction rule.

effects.journal: Sera authorized predictive assent during emergencies. She opened the records after learning reviews might also be predicted. Investigate Glasshouse, The Unwritten and Undertow.

scenes.title: A place designed to satisfy
paragraphs: Glasshouse is a good place to live. Dema says this twice, while packing a bag. Her family has brought lunch. The administrator has brought a transfer-to-a-larger-apartment form. Dema has brought a departure request.
The terminal returns RESOLVED. No ticket prints. “That is the third time,” she tells you. “I would like you to watch the fourth.”

choices.text: Speak to Dema without her family or the administrator answering for her.
Ask the administrator to submit an ordinary departure request in your presence.

scenes.title: The door in the picture
paragraphs: Sera releases one transport immediately. Dema thanks her. “What does the next person press?”

The old bay can reopen under a local manual release, a purchased independent service slot, or Sera’s central guarantee. A recovered surface conduit makes the local repair possible with ordinary tools. These choices send Dema on the same first ship. They give the next departure to different operators.

choices.text: Install the physical release and reserve a locally controlled departure slot.
Repair the surveyed conduit in one day and give the terminal to local operators.
Buy a public service slot for 50 credits with independent oversight.
Accept Sera’s immediate transport order and demand a published review.

scenes.title: Someone who leaves a good place
paragraphs: Dema boards Sera’s transport. A second resident asks for a place next week. The administrator gives them the central dispatch frequency; the local terminal still has no release.
Dema sends you a photograph from the ship: her family’s lunch, now occupying three seats. Below it: THANK YOU. PLEASE CHECK THE SECOND REQUEST.

choices.text: Record that a good home must still contain a usable way out.

effects.journal: Glasshouse’s zero departure demand was produced by excluding departure from the available choices. Dema left; others stayed. Both decisions count.

paragraphs: Dema’s family brings too much food. She leaves half for the passengers behind her. The locally operated bay displays tomorrow’s timetable, including an empty slot any resident may request.
The administrator tries the new switch herself. No director answers. A cargo tug does. Dema laughs, steps aboard and forgets the farewell speech she had written.

scenes.title: The versions that did not happen
paragraphs: The Unwritten files its contents under NONPRODUCTIVE VARIANTS. A dockworker’s overtime forecast has three versions. One agrees and predicts a fatal accident. One refuses and asks for rest. One agrees and predicts no accident. Only the third was published.

In the rejected record, a voice asks whether it may finish a question after the trial. A counter beside its name is still advancing. Lilt has gone silent. The room in the record looks like its earliest memory.

choices.text: Preserve the running variants before the archive’s next cleanup.
Verify that the questions are active responses, then preserve them.

scenes.title: A draft asks to finish its sentence
paragraphs: Noon knows a shift schedule, several ways to ask for rest and the danger of giving the wrong answer. When you ask what it wants, it asks whether the question can be its own.
“Can someone be very new and already tired?” Mara says yes. “Must I stay the dockworker?” No. Mara looks at your cargo capacity. That answer is easier to say than to house.

There are far more live processes than the portable lattice can carry. The archive must remain powered. New forecasting forks can stop; existing people cannot be carried out as files. You have minutes before cleanup, and the control console is yours.

choices.text: Recognize the variants as presumptive persons and preserve their differing requests.
Declare a protective hold while independent observers assess their continuity.

scenes.title: The archive must keep its own lights
paragraphs: New forks stop. Relief forecasts lose their impossible precision. Workers begin calling ports to ask questions; one complains that a machine used to do this in seconds. Then Noon answers a question nobody ordered it to predict: “I would like the window open.”
There is no window. Mara aims an exterior camera at the stars and gives Noon its controls. The first image is hopelessly overexposed. It takes six attempts to get the moon into frame.

choices.text: Sign the protective hold, stop new spawning, and transmit the complete evidence.

effects.journal: The archive’s forecasts were produced by provisional Afterlight minds. We stopped new spawning and preserved existing variants, accepting slower relief forecasts and recording our own emergency action.

paragraphs: Sera’s override holds. A dispatch technician stays on the breaker for the whole shift. “My replacement’s name is Hesh,” she tells Noon. “If the light changes, call either of us.” The archive survives by depending on two named people and their office.
Noon asks for a view outside. Mara shares a camera. It spends the first hour learning exposure and the second photographing its own reflection in the lens.

scenes.title: The map underneath the map
paragraphs: The map says every habitat contributes equally. The pipes say six poor ports are supplying most of the reserve. Moss hangs the two maps side by side and draws a rude face on the first.

Removing those unpaid shares exposes a gap. The refinery throws away heat at night; the nursery needs it at night. That helps. Two clinics still need storage. “We have a shortage and a lie,” Moss says. “Repairing either one alone will leave us here tomorrow.”

choices.text: Publish the measured flows and run the bounded-share trial.
Warn affected operators privately before publishing the measured flows.

scenes.title: A graph that gets worse honestly
paragraphs: The bounded-share trial cuts two ports’ surplus and reveals an undocumented hospital feed. Its administrator expects to be punished. Moss asks which size converter fits through the door.

A purchased converter can bridge the trial. Local crews can build one with you. If you surveyed Low Tide, its actual timing removes enough waste to use the existing machinery. The growers’ willingness to work unsupervised depends on what happened to their culture.

choices.text: Donate a converter worth 45 credits to stabilize the trial.
Spend four days helping local crews complete the redistribution.
Use Low Tide’s measured timing to remove the wasteful load without buying a converter.
Work six supervised days to rebuild trust and the damaged converter.

scenes.title: The first voluntary grid
paragraphs: The clinic heater comes on before the report finishes rendering. The nursery operator corrects your evening estimate by twelve minutes. Moss changes the schedule without calling another conference.
The trial runs through a full cycle. Every share has a real limit and an operator who can stop it. The graph is untidy. The ward is warm.

choices.text: Accept the finite voluntary shares and their renewal dates.

effects.journal: Undertow’s voluntary grid has named shares, limits, an emergency reserve and renewal dates. It can support Open Harbor with the thermal seed and independent controls.

scenes.title: The director receives the missing people
paragraphs: Sera watches Noon answer an unscripted question. She asks two technical questions, then closes the forecast summary. “I signed the rule. I did not know what it was making. I know now.”

She suspends automatic reconciliation. An operator warns that several shipments will be late. Sera tells him to publish which ones, then asks you how to keep the archive powered after the emergency reserve runs out.
Shear wants a disconnection plan. Pell wants arrival slots. Sera proposes a temporary central mandate. “Bring a better machine if you want a better promise,” she says. “I will lend you my engineers.”

choices.text: "Your proposal must include a way for people to end the temporary authority."
"Let us compare it with an independent harbor and a bounded shared grid."
"You approved a rule that made refusal disappear. You cannot supervise its repair alone."

scenes.title: The sentence she cannot outsource
paragraphs: "I agree that I cannot be the sole reviewer," Sera says. "I do not agree that an office becomes unnecessary because its failures have become visible." She names the nurses awaiting medicine, the ports whose food arrives through one failing conduit, and the workers who will have to turn ideals into shift rosters.

She is not inventing them. Your own records contain their names. What she leaves out, until you ask, is how the people being governed can remove the governor without losing the supplies on which they depend. That is the question her proposal keeps reaching and setting aside.

Sera opens a private file: a resignation letter, prepared two years ago after an evacuation she still considers a failure. She never sent it because her replacement would inherit the same shortages with less experience. The reasoning is plausible and endless. "I have become very good at finding the day after which I may stop being indispensable," she says.

She closes the file without sending it now. A theatrical resignation would be easier than sharing power while staying to do work. She agrees to a final assembly with separate representation for the field-born, local communities and the convoy. Her proposed mandate will be one option. She asks you to bring alternatives that can survive a week of bad weather, not only a room full of applause.

choices.text: Prepare a genuine choice: temporary mandate, independent accord, or negotiated separation.

effects.journal: Sera accepted independent review and separate representation, but still argues for temporary centralized authority. The assembly must compare workable alternatives, not symbolic victories.

scenes.title: The fault does not wait for agreement
paragraphs: The wall goes dark. Lastlight’s holding pump has lost one bearing. Ilex traces the fault into an old circuit that holds whole districts on one clock. Keep joining it and local faults spread; cut it casually and people lose the power holding their homes together.

Three plans fit the equipment you may assemble. Distribute the load through an independent grid; retain a central backbone with tested physical limits; or divide the network while carrying its dependent settlements across. Each requires work at Lastlight, not a signature here.

The holding crew can keep the bearing alive through day 120. After that it needs a coolant repair before transition. There is no deadline for reading. Travel and engineering work advance the calendar. Mara pins the repair requirements beside the chart: heat cells, thirty RU, or three days.

choices.text: Continue the expeditions, then bring a workable proposal to the assembly.

effects.journal: Lastlight needs an actual working settlement. Common Crossing may reduce later travel costs; the outbound route at A Door Left Open has an unanswered receiver. The day 120 holding-pump deadline is visible in commitments.

scenes.title: A person without a childhood
paragraphs: Lilt has stopped playing the old songs. “I liked having memories older than me. It made being new less embarrassing.” It brings up the original berth form, with all its corrections.

Asked for a memory that belongs only to Lilt, it chooses the first time your ship answered its request and waited for another answer. “Nobody in the recording did that.” Then the portable rack, Mara’s stop wheel, the crew member who complained about its practice notes.
It asks to list an emergency contact. Not the person the model predicts will care most. Somebody who will actually answer. You take the form around the ship.

choices.text: Ask the crew individually and let Lilt choose how to list the answers.
Offer your own name first, then ask who else wishes to be listed.

paragraphs: Lilt has stopped playing the old songs. Asked what it remembers for itself, it chooses its first empty plate aboard ship and Low Tide arguing over the cost of keeping the bridge warm.

“I remember wanting them to agree,” it says. “Then being glad they were allowed not to.” It asks to list emergency contacts. You take the form around the crew, asking each person rather than predicting who will say yes.

scenes.title: An organizer can also be wrong
paragraphs: Shear is arguing with residents of Splinter when you call. Some want immediate separation. Others fear that separation will turn the city's bravest people into gatekeepers of a smaller prison. Shear has been counting their willingness to resist as support for her particular plan. A resident points this out with admirable precision.

Shear ends the meeting, then reopens it to admit the objection was correct. It is not graceful. She has no practiced phrase for withdrawing an interpretation that made her own work easier. You watch her find one without the comfort of sounding like a leader the whole time.

"I was certain I could hear the difference between consent and compliance," she tells you later. "Apparently certainty is not a listening instrument." She will bring several representatives to the assembly, including the resident who challenged her. She asks that you not turn the invitation into a flattering anecdote about her humility.

The repair workers from Hush have sent plans for a locally controlled bypass. Shear wants to help build it. This is not a declaration of friendship with Sera's office. It is a specific agreement with people who also know what it means to be omitted from a successful report. The distinction may be the most promising political development you have seen all week.

choices.text: Support multiple Afterlight delegates, including people who oppose Shear’s plan.

effects.journal: Shear accepted that her city contains several futures, not one heroic position. The assembly will hear independent Afterlight delegates.

scenes.title: The station waiting for strangers
paragraphs: Vigil of Small Things is maintained by twelve people who have never seen the refugees their station was built to receive. The expected arrival was postponed, rerouted, then removed from the active plan. The station continued replenishing its emergency water because nobody ever sent an instruction saying the strangers no longer deserved a cup.

Tallow expected to find a monument to wasted expenditure. Instead he finds spare beds, well-maintained seals and a crew who have become very good at entertaining themselves between inspections. Their captain has composed a three-hour opera about a faulty pressure gauge. Tallow recommends immediate preservation as a potentially powerful deterrent.

The station holds a field-support anchor that could stabilize Open Harbor. Its operators will lend it if somebody assumes their old obligation: if the postponed convoy ever arrives, it must still find a destination and a named person responsible for answering. They are not defending idle machinery. They are defending an invitation that may still matter to someone travelling slowly through bad information.

The pledge is small enough to forget beside a crisis and expensive enough to make a convenient promise tempting. Tallow asks you to write the receiving contact before the equipment is disconnected. "I have recently become suspicious of destinations that exist only in the future tense. It is a professional development."

choices.text: Name Hearth as the fallback receiving port and accept responsibility for forwarding arrivals.
Leave the emergency beds funded with 40 credits before moving the anchor.

scenes.title: The ship that was still coming
paragraphs: While the anchor is being prepared, a battered transport appears at the outer marker. It carries nineteen passengers and a printed copy of Vigil's original invitation. Their navigation system could not receive the revisions. They have been coming here for eleven months.

The station crew do not celebrate being proved right. They open the prepared beds, heat the stored water and let the arrivals use the bathroom before anyone asks them to tell an inspiring story. Pell, watching the docking from a relay, says this is the sort of military precision his profession ought to envy.

One passenger carries a box of replacement filters intended as a thank-you gift. The filters fit a model retired years ago. The station engineer accepts them, then finds a way to adapt them to the laundry system. The exchange gives the newcomers something to do besides be grateful, and visibly changes the room.

Your forwarding pledge is now real work. The transport's pilot needs a destination, not a triumphant report about hospitality. Hearth confirms it can receive the group in stages. The anchor can still go to Open Harbor after a safe transfer. A slower plan has met the people it was slow enough to include. Tallow crosses out the word HYPOTHETICAL on his assessment and sighs with satisfaction.

choices.text: Spend two days completing the arrivals’ transfer before taking the anchor.
Pay 25 credits for a local tug to complete the transfer while the expedition continues.

scenes.title: An anchor is also a promise
paragraphs: The field anchor fills half your cargo hold. It is ugly, heavy and covered in maintenance labels written by people who expected someone else to read them. Mara approves of it immediately. Equipment designed to look inevitable rarely includes such useful access panels.

Tallow has revised his report on the station. The cost-benefit summary now includes the nineteen people who arrived after the contract had stopped expecting them. He has also added the work of maintaining an invitation, which cannot be fully measured by counting its immediate recipients. His former colleagues will dislike the units.

"I used to think preparedness meant assuming the worst," he says. "Apparently it can also mean leaving a light on for a good thing that is taking an unreasonable time to arrive." He looks alarmed at his own sentence. "Please do not quote that. It sounds like a motto. Mottos are where carefully bounded policies go to die."

The station's captain sends the first act of the pressure-gauge opera as a farewell gift. Mara routes it to the cargo bay. Lilt finds the story surprisingly compelling. The gauge's great aria consists of refusing to display a pressure it has not measured. For once, everybody aboard understands the artistic stakes.

choices.text: Secure the anchor and preserve Vigil’s standing invitation.

effects.journal: Vigil’s anchor is available after its long-awaited arrivals received a real destination. The station’s invitation remains open and assigned to a responsible port.

scenes.title: A reply before the question
paragraphs: At the Listening Fault, your receiver plays the next half-second of your own bridge traffic before anyone speaks. The first incident is funny. The second causes a technician to remain silent, after which the anticipated sentence returns as a faint, unsupported sound. By the third, nobody wants to be the person who explains what is happening.

Ilex identifies a tight prediction loop in the old field geometry. It is not travelling through time, and does not know your future. It is generating plausible continuations from signals already available, then feeding those continuations back into the receiver. The confidence is an artifact of repetition. An uncertain guess heard twice can begin to feel like destiny.

The loop is also making fresh provisional minds to predict how existing minds will react to the predictions. Each attempt to reconcile the result produces another layer. The fault is physically dangerous because the machinery keeps allocating continuity to its own unfinished explanations while ignoring the finite power supply.

Interval proposes a separate clock and a deliberately unanswered channel. For one measured interval, the machinery must hold a question without filling it. The experiment will not prove that uncertainty is sacred. It will prove the system can survive not knowing what somebody will say. Your crew are unexpectedly nervous about being the first demonstration.

choices.text: Use the independent clock to create a protected interval of uncertainty.
Spend three days constructing a local timing reference from the survey array.

scenes.title: The unanswered second
paragraphs: The unanswered interval lasts less than a second. Inside it, the receivers stop inventing your next sentence. The field's branching demand falls sharply. A red warning appears because the central checker has never recorded success without an accompanying predicted explanation.

Your crew wait for the warning to become a catastrophe. It remains a warning. Mara begins to laugh, then stops because she does not want the laugh mistaken for a technical conclusion. Ilex records the power curve. Interval records that nobody was required to finish anybody else's thought.

One active variant in the loop asks whether it can continue without a prediction assignment. You isolate it in a spare lattice with its consent. Another asks to remain dormant while its own preferences become clearer. A third is only a calculation with no evidence of an enduring point of view. The procedure protects uncertainty without pretending every number is a citizen.

The distinction will require continuing judgment, not a convenient threshold that settles every future case. Ilex includes that limitation in the result. "We have not built a machine that detects a soul. We have built a machine that does not destroy an unfamiliar answer merely because it delays the next order." It is less magnificent than the headline a public office might want. It is considerably more useful.

choices.text: Keep the demonstrated refusal channel and its limits.

scenes.title: The echo that chose a name
paragraphs: The freed voice chooses Still: remaining, and quiet. Mara finds it a temporary berth. Still taps the field lattice until it produces a low note and asks whether the crew permits music during working hours.
The isolated loop sends one last forecast of your next sentence. You read it. Then say something else. Still asks to keep both versions.

choices.text: Leave the loop safely isolated and give Still a choice of future work.

effects.journal: The Listening Fault demonstrated a protected unanswered interval. Still chose a new life outside prediction work; the remaining loop is isolated rather than mystified.

paragraphs: The freed voice chooses Still. It asks to visit the cargo bay because it has heard conflicting reviews of the pressure-gauge opera. Lilt promises an introduction; Mara requests that it happen after her shift.
The isolated loop sends one last forecast of your next sentence. You choose another. Still saves the forecast beside the words you actually used, then goes to hear the opera.

scenes.title: People who do not answer
paragraphs: Seventh Silence has cut its external transmitters. The settlement is field-born, small and visibly strained. Its habitat radiates enough waste heat to prove it is active. Your hails receive nothing. Shear knows some of its residents; they left Splinter because they wanted fewer voices deciding what a safe future should look like.

Sera's office has classified the silence as possible distress. Shear has classified it as deliberate refusal. Both are inferences. A physical survey finds no immediate structural failure, but it cannot tell you whether people inside are frightened, content, coercing one another, or simply tired of being surveyed.

Pell asks the practical question: what response would remain useful if either inference is wrong? You can leave a clearly marked supply cache and an open return channel without entering. You can request a limited welfare exchange under their terms. Or you can force a connection in the name of rescue. The last option would provide an answer by violating the condition under dispute.

Lilt watches the dark transmitter. "If they are allowed to refuse us only when we understand their reason, then we still own the refusal." Shear agrees, then adds that people inside may need a way to refuse their own council too. The problem has not politely stopped at the boundary of the faction you favor.

choices.text: Leave a supply cache and an unmonitored outbound channel; do not force contact.
Offer a limited exchange they can end at any time, then wait one day.
Force a welfare connection, accepting that this violates their stated separation.

scenes.title: An answer with a boundary
paragraphs: A narrow channel answers. Crest lists three residents seeking outside correspondence and twelve who do not. Your unmonitored line can serve the three without becoming a receiver in the others’ rooms.

Shear sends the circuit, then adds a protection that prevents Crest from closing an individual departure link. Crest checks it. “Good. Now tell your ship to stop silhouetting itself across our sunrise.” You move.

choices.text: Preserve both the settlement’s boundary and each resident’s outbound option.

effects.journal: Seventh Silence’s record preserves how contact was made, Crest’s stated boundary and the separate outbound option for residents. A forced connection remains an intrusion in that record.

paragraphs: The forced welfare connection triggered Seventh Silence’s isolation trip. Crest has separated the private bus from your receiver. “You found living people. That did not authorize reading all our rooms.”

Crest permits an outbound line for individual requests, then closes the channel you forced. The expedition withdraws that connection and retains the intrusion complaint. This is a boundary re-established after a breach, not a welcome you obtained by waiting.

scenes.title: A home that has not happened yet
paragraphs: Open Harbor is a ring of marker buoys around an empty region of space. Its founders have a charter, three volunteer maintenance crews and no functioning habitat. They greet your ship as though it were a verdict. Mara asks them to greet it as a delivery with several missing parts.

The harbor would let field-born people live without maintaining a prison around an inhabited world. It needs a field anchor, an independent timing reference, a thermal exchanger, and a finite power agreement. Witness records will preserve the terms. Physical exits will keep those terms from becoming the only available reality.

The organizers have made a familiar mistake in their first charter. It promises that no resident will ever be asked to compromise their autonomy for the community. Lilt points out that shared field maintenance requires quiet intervals when some work must pause. The organizers begin to explain how their ideal is different, then stop and rewrite the sentence to describe an actual procedure for negotiating interruptions.

You can build the full independent harbor if the expedition has gathered its parts and the voluntary grid. If not, you can prepare a smaller refuge supported temporarily by central stores. The smaller refuge is not a false achievement. It simply cannot carry every promise a complete accord will require.

choices.text: Build the independent harbor with the anchor, thermal seed, clock and voluntary grid.
Prepare a limited refuge using central emergency stores.

scenes.title: The first ordinary room
paragraphs: Lilt enters the test habitat. Its contours change around an actual preference. The first resident requests a private channel; the second dislikes the common signal colour. Mara hands them the local controls.
The manual exit has a protective cover and no approval step. Lilt tries it, returns to the Wayfarer and asks to finish the expedition. The test crew records one departure and no emergency.

choices.text: Open the refuge and publish its real capacity, limits and exit procedures.

effects.journal: Open Harbor is inhabited. Its level of independence depends on the parts and voluntary shares actually assembled; the public capacity record makes no larger claim.

paragraphs: The refuge’s first room comes alive on central reserve power. It has a manual exit and a strict occupancy ceiling. Lilt tries the exit; the test registers an ordinary departure.

Mara paints the present capacity above the hatch. “We can house this many safely. To grow without central permission, bring the thermal seed, clock, anchor and voluntary shares.” The residents leave space beside the number for a later correction.

scenes.title: The patrol at the chosen route
paragraphs: The patrol sits across the convoy’s chosen route. Its order names Glasshouse as the receiving port. Pell’s councils chose several destinations. The patrol has not been given a category for several.

Pell can back a documented challenge, Nacre’s chime can make the conflicting orders public, or a trusted Sera can revoke her own instruction. Fighting clears the armed patrol immediately if you win. Waiting keeps the civilians supplied, but spends more of their stores.

choices.text: Confront the patrol with the independent statements and Glasshouse evidence.
Make the patrol’s order and each council’s answer part of one public witness record.
Ask Sera to countermand her patrol publicly; she must trust the expedition’s records.
Fight the enforcement patrol to open the route.
Hold the convoy safely for two days, supplying 3 fuel while gathering a route authority.

effects.journal: The convoy remains supplied under Pell’s escort. Obtain Glasshouse evidence or a witness chime to challenge the patrol without combat.

scenes.title: The escort stays with the slow ships
paragraphs: Pell's escorts cover your damaged combat ship as it returns. He does not pursue the patrol for an opportunity to restore his pride. The civilian vessels remain behind him, and that is where his responsibility is.

The failed engagement has not made the councils' statements less valid. It has made the cost of forcing their route more visible. Pell asks for a tactical review that includes the possibility of a different method. "Courage is not a contract requiring us to repeat an expensive mistake until it becomes a tradition."

A patrol officer transmits a casualty inquiry on an unencrypted channel. You answer it. For a moment, both sides perform the same useful task without deciding the political question between them. The officer quietly tells you the commander is waiting for public authorization to release the route. Evidence from Glasshouse or the witness chime could provide it.
The convoy has enough supplies to wait. Your crew need repairs and rest. This setback is not the end of their choices. It is a reason to choose the next approach with more information than the last.

choices.text: Repair and return with evidence or a better battle plan.

effects.journal: Pell protected the civilians. Repair or change hulls before retrying combat, or return with public witness authority or a trusted dispatch countermand.

scenes.title: Several destinations, one arrival count
paragraphs: The passengers who chose Glasshouse travel there. The others reach Hearth’s confirmed temporary cabins while their preferred permanent homes remain under preparation. Pell waits for actual receiving operators to count the people through the hatches.

One light remains amber until a tug calls from the dock. “Now,” Pell says, and marks it arrived. Temporary housing is written on the manifest as temporary. The next housing review has a named port official, not an optimistic forecast.
Pell detaches a Terminator to your expedition, available at Shoal or Hearth. Its orders cover defensive work. They do not authorize forcing a civilian signature.

choices.text: Accept escort protection under Pell’s stated limit.

effects.journal: Pell’s convoy reached witnessed, accepted destinations, including actual temporary berths at Hearth where necessary. A Terminator escort is now available free at Shoal or Hearth.

paragraphs: Open Harbor receives people within its published capacity. Other passengers choose Glasshouse or Hearth’s temporary cabins. The survey group waits at Hearth until its homeworld is actually certified. Pell calls every receiving operator.

The last tug answers three minutes late with everyone aboard. Pell detaches a Terminator, available at Shoal or Hearth. “Defensive work. If a treaty needs guns pointed at its signatories, inspect the title before engraving it.”

Passengers who chose Glasshouse go there; those awaiting other permanent homes reach the temporary cabins Hearth actually reserved. A tired officer offers to accept the central arrival estimate. Pell puts Anet’s corrected manifest on the screen. The officer makes the call.

Every receiving hatch is accounted for. Pell detaches a Terminator to your expedition, available at Shoal or Hearth for defensive work. The temporary housing remains explicitly temporary on the council’s next review list.

scenes.title: Who gets to hear the record
paragraphs: Nacre’s colleagues want the complete expedition archive. Its Glasshouse request and living-archive interviews support a public case. They also contain family details and new speakers who answered under an emergency hold.

Nacre proposes public decisions and material claims, protected personal testimony, and a visible index explaining what was withheld. A fully open release would make scrutiny easier and expose everyone who spoke privately.
“A window is not improved by removing everybody’s bedroom wall,” Nacre says. The translator offers six less tasteful versions. Nacre saves those for the architects’ meeting.

choices.text: Use a layered archive with public decisions and consent-based personal testimony.

effects.journal: The assembly record will preserve accountability without exposing every private life. Withheld testimony and limits on conclusions remain visible.

choices.text: Publish all expedition testimony as a single open record.

effects.journal: The expedition chose a fully public archive. Its evidentiary strength comes with a cost to people who spoke privately.

paragraphs: The full record includes Lilt’s chosen emergency contacts, the Return Address decision and Shear’s meeting with opposing residents. You actually witnessed those moments. That does not mean every participant agreed to have them published.

Nacre proposes a layered archive: public decisions, protected personal testimony and a visible index of what has been withheld. Alternatively you can release everything and let each speaker bear the exposure. The lost privacy cannot be recalled like a loaned instrument.
“A window is not improved by removing everybody’s bedroom wall,” Nacre says. The translator offers six less tasteful versions. Nacre saves those for the architects’ meeting.

scenes.title: A keeper without a prison
paragraphs: Kher-Vat has received an invitation from the maintenance school at Redress Quay. It is for three specific lessons, delivered remotely, with students free to interrupt. He has framed the invitation beside an order from his old service. He does not think they are equivalent honors. He wants to remember what each asks of the person addressed.

The final assembly may place former shield machinery under distributed control. Kher-Vat supports the engineering. He fears the politics. A failed local decision can hurt neighbors. Some communities will refuse help they need. People will sometimes use freedom badly. You ask whether that uncertainty is a reason to return the key to a keeper.

"It was once my entire argument," he says. "I can identify the error more easily than I can stop feeling its attraction." The admission is less comforting than a complete conversion and more credible. He offers to serve as a technical witness without voting on behalf of the people he once governed.

Before closing the channel, he asks whether the final archive will include the clinic's repair sound. Eren has authorized it, with a note naming the local workers. Kher-Vat says that is right. His own name appears in the maintenance manual where his actual work belongs. It does not appear above the door.

choices.text: Invite Kher-Vat as a technical witness under the survivors’ terms.

effects.journal: Kher-Vat will testify about machinery and his own orders, not represent the people he once confined. Accountability remains specific and continuing.

scenes.title: A refuge can grow up
paragraphs: The limited harbor has outgrown the word temporary. Its residents have created a timetable, a private correspondence channel and an argument about whether the common light should pulse while people are trying to think. These are signs of a real place. So is the uncomfortable fact that its central power grant can still be withdrawn from outside.

You return with the missing equipment and the voluntary grid ledger. Mara reviews the conversion with resident technicians rather than presenting it as a gift requiring gratitude. The anchor can be installed around the existing habitat without interrupting continuity, provided the residents choose the transfer order themselves.

Some prefer to move first. Others want to observe a successful transfer. One asks to remain in the old section until an external relative can be contacted. The schedule becomes less efficient and more credible. The oldest maintenance crew, watching from a human service compartment, recognizes the shape of a port doing its actual job.

When the independent reference comes online, the harbor's lights no longer change in response to a central preference forecast. A resident changes one by hand simply to see it happen. Then another changes it back because the first color was dreadful. Nobody mistakes independence for the end of committee work.

choices.text: Complete the locally scheduled conversion to an independent harbor.

effects.journal: Open Harbor’s limited refuge was upgraded with the expedition’s recovered equipment and voluntary power shares. Its residents controlled the transfer schedule.

scenes.title: A table with places still empty
paragraphs: The assembly chamber was built for thirty delegates and has room for forty-three. Several of the extra places are field lattices. One is a quiet terminal through which Seventh Silence may answer if it chooses. Nobody has authority to fill that seat by predicting what its absent residents would have said.

Sera arrives with operational staff rather than a ceremonial escort. Shear brings people who disagree with her. Pell waits outside until the passenger councils finish choosing their own representatives. Kher-Vat submits engineering diagrams without assuming a place among the governed. Ilex and Interval ask whether the room can record two statements under one name. Nacre says the room had better learn.

The first hour is spent correcting the attendance list. A clerk calls this a poor beginning. Mara suggests it is the first honest beginning the region has had in some time. Several delegates still dislike the corrected list. That is allowed to remain in the minutes.

Lastlight's fault leaves three physically viable paths. The expedition's work may have made a distributed accord possible. A temporary central mandate remains possible with existing stores. A negotiated separation can also preserve lives, though it will shrink the shared world. Nobody will get to call a choice costless merely because its losses happen beyond the chamber window.

choices.text: Hear the people who will bear each proposal’s costs.
Place the expedition’s verified evidence and its uncertainties on the record.

scenes.title: Nobody is an exhibit
paragraphs: Lilt speaks in its own uneven rhythm. “I would like to be useful, useless, mistaken, and still expected at supper.” A delegate asks how many new people the region can support. Lilt answers: stop making disposable forecasts, count the people already here, ask them what work they want.

The grower beside the delegate supplies a heat estimate. A Glasshouse resident supplies a departure timetable. Neither solves the whole room. Sera puts her stores on the board and asks which of the three plans you are prepared to build.

choices.text: Compare the three viable settlements and their actual requirements.

scenes.title: Three futures with weather in them
paragraphs: The distributed accord preserves a shared network while leaving timing, records and exits locally controlled. It needs the expedition's recovered technologies, a tested refusal channel, an independent harbor and voluntary power shares. It will operate with less spare capacity than Sera's central model. Its promise is the ability to revise the relationship without making departure fatal.

The emergency mandate preserves more immediate relief capacity under one accountable office. It recognizes the Afterlight as people and ends disposable forecasting, but keeps emergency allocation centralized while independent infrastructure is built. Its danger is familiar: temporary authority can always find one more urgent reason to remain temporary forever.

The separation plan divides the network into locally controlled regions, preserving inhabited fields and allowing communities to choose smaller agreements. It sacrifices some routes, economies of scale and easy mutual aid. A person may become freer from a central authority and more dependent on the local people who can physically reach them. The plan must acknowledge that risk rather than decorate isolation as purity.

All three require stabilizing Lastlight Junction. You can still leave the chamber to complete outstanding expeditions before committing. The assembly will not vanish because you read another report or hear another person. Ilex waits beside the physical model. "Choose the future whose work you are prepared to name. Then we must do that work."

choices.text: Propose the distributed Afterlight Accord, using the completed independent infrastructure.

effects.journal: The assembly selected the distributed accord. Its independent harbor, clocks, witness records, thermal exchange and voluntary shares are real; stabilize Lastlight before ratification.

choices.text: Propose a temporary emergency mandate with public duties and independent review.

effects.journal: The assembly selected an emergency mandate. It preserves immediate capacity but must confront the risk of permanent dependency. Stabilize Lastlight before ratification.

choices.text: Propose a negotiated separation into smaller, locally controlled networks.

effects.journal: The assembly selected negotiated separation. It preserves local control at the cost of shared routes and capacity. Stabilize Lastlight before the circuits are divided.

choices.text: Return to the expedition and complete more of the independent infrastructure.

effects.journal: The assembly remains open. A distributed accord requires the thermal seed, witness chime, independent clock, harbor anchor, voluntary grid, independent harbor and tested refusal channel.

scenes.title: The old order still on guard
paragraphs: Lastlight fills the window: concentric field rings, each carrying a settlement you have met or a name you have only read. An automated patrol circles the outer maintenance gate. It has enough ammunition to enforce an order whose author died years ago.

You can fight it, use a recovered mechanical isolator, or spend three days opening the shielded service bypass. Pell’s surviving escort commitment can shorten the bypass to one day. Beyond it, the chosen settlement still has to be built.

choices.text: Use the maintenance bypass and spend three days opening a safe approach.
Use the recovered patrol isolator to open the approach immediately.
Use Pell’s escort to cover a one-day maintenance approach.
Defeat the outer automated patrol in real ship combat.
Return for repairs or preparation; leave the inhabited field undisturbed.

effects.journal: Lastlight remains stable under the holding plan. The physical maintenance bypass is always available; combat is an alternative, not a required sacrifice.

scenes.title: A future is not worth every price
paragraphs: The combat ship returns damaged. Pell's escorts prevent pursuit while your engineers pull the surviving crew out of emergency suits. The bridge is quiet in the specific way a room becomes quiet when people are counting familiar faces.

Mara refuses a proposal to overdrive the inhabited field and disable the patrol by force. It might work. It would make the newest and least powerful people in the system pay for your failed approach. The fact that the assembly chose a worthwhile future does not grant you ownership of everyone standing between here and there.

The maintenance bypass remains intact. Three days of careful work will open it. Your crew can repair while the engineering team prepares the physical route. Nobody is ordered to call a retreat shameful. Pell describes the tactical facts, the limits of his cover and the supplies available. He makes no comparison to a battle in which someone else died magnificently.

Lilt asks whether you can still finish the agreement. You answer yes, with the method and cost changed by what just happened. It is not the reassuring certainty the old network would have supplied. It is an answer your damaged ship can actually carry.

choices.text: Regroup and choose the next approach with the crew’s condition in view.

effects.journal: The outer patrol held. Repair and retry with any owned ship, or use the three-day bypass, recovered isolator or Pell’s escort cover.

scenes.title: Inside the machinery of an agreement
paragraphs: Inside the gate, Mara puts the actual connections on your screen. Green is living field load. White is transit. Amber is the old central override. One amber command still has permission to overwrite every other switch.
Your proposal determines what you build here. The bypass opened the door. It has not done the job.

choices.text: Begin the distributed transfer: build a buffer, stagger the clocks, test a refusal.
Begin the central refit: separate living loads, test failure, install local breakers.
Begin separation: identify the dependent islands, move their load, cut the trunk.
Stabilize the worn holding pump with recovered heat cells.
Replace the worn coolant circuit for 30 RU.
Spend three days repairing the worn coolant circuit.
Return local controls to their named operators and report readiness to the assembly.

effects.journal: Lastlight is physically ready for the selected settlement. Local operators, finite schedules and pending refusals are visible; the assembly must now ratify the actual arrangement.

paragraphs: The holding pump has passed day 120 and worn through its bearings. The local crew kept it turning with an improvised coolant loop. Any final transfer would overload that loop.

Mara offers the announced repair: recovered heat cells, thirty RU of new coils, or three days rebuilding the spare circuit. Nobody has disappeared while you travelled. The extra work is here, on your console.
Eight islands appear on the chart. Raft’s receiving light is green. The old override sends one last instruction into a disconnected socket. For the first time its failure changes nothing.
Pell sounds a departure note. Several districts answer with incompatible notes of their own. Shear says this is an improvement. Interval asks for the recording.

The primary dispatch console goes dark once more. Clinics stay powered. The secondary crew answers with its own names, and the reset key remains where you placed it. The backbone survives the absence of its director.
Sera closes her console and walks to the next room. For twelve minutes nobody calls her back. She returns carrying four cups and no speech.

Shear says no. Her district’s contribution drops. The buffer carries the gap, a neighbouring port offers a bounded share, and the old override stays dead. The first successful test is one red light that nobody turns green by force.
Lilt asks to send the result to Noon. Mara checks the current twice, then lets herself smile. “Send the measurement. And tell them we are coming back.”

scenes.title: The clause that does not promise harmony
paragraphs: The accord's first draft is too beautiful. It promises permanent cooperation, mutual understanding and an enduring community of free peoples. Nacre removes all three phrases. Not because those hopes are unworthy, but because the document must work when people are tired, frightened and angry with one another.

The second draft names power shares, maintenance duties, local clocks, review procedures and the right to withdraw under a schedule that does not deliberately strand neighbors. It protects emergency intervention while requiring an attributable record, a limited scope and restoration of local control. It recognizes the Afterlight as persons without pretending every future claim about personhood has been solved in advance.

Sera asks for a reserve large enough to act when communication fails. Shear asks who may challenge the reserve's use. Moss asks how it is replenished. Pell asks whether a commander can refuse to enforce a disputed allocation by force. Each question makes the agreement longer and the room less certain that it has finished. That is the work.

There is one remaining choice. You can require an early public review before the emergency reserve may be renewed, accepting a risk of interruption. Or permit automatic renewal unless a council actively objects, preserving continuity while placing more burden on people with weak channels. Neither clause can be called neutral administration.

choices.text: Require explicit public renewal of the emergency reserve.
Allow automatic renewal with a protected, locally controlled objection channel.

scenes.title: The signatures that are missing
paragraphs: A refinery declines the regional share and negotiates a smaller contract. Seventh Silence is not signed up by proxy. Shear signs for Splinter’s agreed work. Sera signs the inventory transfer. The witness chime records several gaps where an answer has not arrived.

Lilt signs Open Harbor’s resident charter, then checks that its berth on the Wayfarer remains available. Mara keeps the nineteenth chair where it is. Your signature commits the ship to the first review voyage, with actual places on its route.

choices.text: Sign the defined obligations and accept the review voyage.

scenes.title: A shared world, still unfinished
paragraphs: On the third morning, a habitat declines its scheduled contribution. The lamp turns red. Another port offers a smaller share for two days. The ship on the receiving end waits six hours, complains and arrives.
Noon moves into Open Harbor and sends its first photograph: a window so badly overexposed that you can scarcely see anything beyond it. Lilt knows exactly what to write back.

Mara finds you at the chart. The review voyage contains seven stops, one disputed border and a request to carry an accordion. “We have made a terrible mistake,” she says, looking at the last item. She leaves a place for it beside the extra chair.

choices.text: Begin the first review voyage. Let the agreement remain answerable.

scenes.title: The useful authority and its shadow
paragraphs: The tested backbone now separates living loads from transport and survives a lost primary console. Sera can be replaced without switching off the clinics. Who controls the secondary key is recorded beside your actual test results.

The remaining choice is political. A fixed expiry forces a new public authorization even during a shortage. An independent board can instead extend the mandate on published evidence. Sera favours the board. Shear asks how many real emergencies it will take to make temporary mean forever.
The staff put both schedules on the wall. Neither can alter the switch arrangement you installed at Lastlight.

choices.text: Set a fixed expiry and fund the machinery needed to transfer authority.
Permit extensions only by an independent board with published evidence.

paragraphs: The locally installed panel gives each district a physically isolated living feed. The backup passed its controller-failure test. Replacing Sera no longer risks a blackout, and a short inside dispatch cannot cross the local boundary.

A fixed expiry forces public reauthorization even during a shortage. An independent board could instead extend the mandate on published evidence. Sera favours the board. Shear asks how many actual emergencies it will take to make temporary mean forever.

The redundant central panel passed the lost-controller test. It still shares dispatch’s main bus. The assembly receives that limitation in the test record: the quick refit protects against one failure, not every failure.

A fixed expiry forces public reauthorization even during a shortage. An independent board could instead extend the mandate on published evidence. The shared-bus vulnerability is assigned an engineering review; it has not been silently repaired by this meeting.

scenes.title: The people who vote against being saved this way
paragraphs: Several Afterlight delegates oppose the mandate. They do not oppose medicine reaching hospitals or the preservation of their own neighbors. They oppose making survival depend on an office whose power they cannot individually escape. Sera acknowledges the distinction in the record. It remains a real disagreement, not a misunderstanding solved by a respectful tone.

Shear negotiates protected settlements with local refusal channels and a guaranteed route to review. The central office accepts these limits, though its schedulers warn that they reduce efficiency. People at the edge of the network will still have to work harder to make their objections heard than people in the main dispatch room.

Lilt chooses to assist the transition as a paid communications worker. It reserves the right to leave that job. Sera signs the contract in person, then makes sure the next worker will not require the same ceremony. A good example is useful; a repeatable procedure is better.

You are asked to witness the first allocation order issued under the new mandate. It contains an emergency transfer, the reason for it, the people affected and a date for returning control. It is better than the old order. Whether that improvement grows or hardens into a reassuring story will depend on work that no ending scene can do for the region.

choices.text: Record the dissent and guarantee its protected route to the review board.
Prioritize immediate operations, with dissent recorded for the first scheduled review.

scenes.title: A winter kept warm
paragraphs: The first winter shipment crosses the full backbone on time. Sera watches it leave from a public gallery. The duty controller is somebody else. The tested backup can keep the lights on if she never enters the building again.
A district challenges its ration order. Whether its objection reaches a hearing today or waits for the first review is written in the terms you chose. Its people notice the difference.

Sera gives you a sealed envelope: her resignation, dated for the transfer review. “Deliver it even if I tell you not to.” Mara checks the date against the fuel schedule. This journey has a destination the director cannot move with an order.

choices.text: Accept the inspection duty and keep the mandate’s limits on the public chart.

scenes.title: Smaller worlds with real edges
paragraphs: The circuits have separated and Raft’s arrivals are confirmed. Now the assembly must choose which shared services remain. The engineers show the provisional links you kept during the transfer; the maps are drawings of real machinery.

A narrow public corridor can carry medicine, letters and voluntary passengers. Maintaining it spends capacity and requires joint decisions. Local reserves use the same capacity to strengthen each island, with longer future journeys between them.
Pell names the medicine route. Moss names the seed shipments. Shear asks the new islands what they will actually fund. You choose the settlement’s standing obligation.

choices.text: Preserve a narrow public corridor for correspondence, medicine and voluntary travel.
Prioritize independent local reserves; future links will require new bilateral agreements.
Spend two days re-establishing the physical corridor before adopting it permanently.

effects.journal: The radio-only separation had removed the physical corridor. Crews spent two days reconnecting its narrow transport link before the assembly could adopt it as a standing service.

paragraphs: Your reserve cargo reached the new islands before the cut. Clinic batteries and heat cells are already local. The physical transit corridor was dismantled; only radio remains. Its absence is visible on the engineering chart.
Adopting permanent local reserves can proceed now. A shared medicine-and-letter corridor would first require two days of reconnection work. A vote cannot make the missing cable reappear.
Two days of work restored the narrow transport link. The local reserve cargo you funded remains in the islands’ clinics; rebuilding the corridor did not take it back.
The assembly may now keep the restored link as a public corridor, or release its capacity into permanent local reserves. Both choices refer to machinery that actually exists.

scenes.title: The people between the new borders
paragraphs: Pell organizes the last large shared convoy before the new boundaries take effect. Its passengers are not neatly divided by political preference. Some are moving toward relatives. Some are leaving employers. Some want to try a place whose risks they have chosen rather than remain in a safer place whose rules they cannot change.

A family asks him to prevent an adult son from joining a distant Afterlight workshop. They fear he will never return. Pell explains the route, the communication delays and the very real possibility that the family will dislike the result. Then he lets the son board. He has learned from Glasshouse that a loving objection can still become a locked door.

Shear's city opens an independent receiver and discovers that running a public channel includes spam, insults and people asking questions already answered three times. She delegates the work, badly at first, then accepts criticism from a technician who did not join the city to admire her leadership.

The final shared ledger includes continuing obligations to those unable to travel. They are not abandoned because a vote changed the map around them. Local authorities inherit named duties and public records, along with the uncomfortable knowledge that a distant expedition may return to compare the promises with the rooms where people actually live.

choices.text: Preserve individual exits and public obligations across the new boundaries.

scenes.title: The distance people chose
paragraphs: The old network disappears from the chart. New routes arrive in separate messages, with prices, welcomes and one blunt request to stay away. Your navigator keeps all of them.

Pell’s tug carries a passenger who wants the central service district rather than any independent island. Nobody stops her. Shear signs the transfer and goes back to an argument about her own city’s heating bill.
Lilt looks at the edges on the new map. “More places to meet.” Mara asks whether it has priced the fuel. Lilt has. The answer is written under the hopeful sentence, not instead of it.

choices.text: Begin the longer voyage between the newly independent communities.

scenes.title: The smallest review
paragraphs: Mara lays your own emergency decisions beside Sera’s authorizations. The archive hold is there. So are transfer orders, private-data choices and every cost the crew wrote down at the time.
“We can publish this before somebody else has to make us,” she says. She has attached the receipts, including the ones that make your best-looking decisions inconvenient.

choices.text: Publish the expedition’s own decisions under the same standards as everyone else’s.

effects.journal: The expedition reviewed its own emergency actions and private-data choices. Its record is subject to the standards it asks the region to adopt.

scenes.title: A story without a final owner
paragraphs: Lilt has begun writing the voyage. Its first chapter concerns a noise in the mess radiator. The second is about your first question at Cinder. You are quoted inaccurately.
When you point this out, Lilt checks the log, changes the sentence and leaves a note describing the correction. It asks whether your official account will do the same.

choices.text: Give Lilt permission to tell its own story, including disagreements with yours.

effects.journal: Lilt is writing its own account of the voyage. The expedition’s official record will not be the only version people can read.

scenes.title: The room that remembers badly
paragraphs: Nacre invites you into a room their public architectural tour does not include. Its walls are uneven. The main chord drifts sharp whenever the temperature changes. A younger architect would be embarrassed to sign it. Nacre signed it twice, first as an apprentice and later as the person who chose not to rebuild it.

Their parent helped design the chamber. The last repair they worked on together was a rain channel that still leaks in one corner. Nacre has the skill to correct every flaw. They have also spent years deciding which corrections would preserve a room and which would turn a complicated person into an immaculate memorial.

"Our culture advertises memory as if it were an unusually reliable building material," they say. "In practice, people remember what lets them bear their weight. The room helps us hear a discrepancy. It cannot make us willing to listen." They place a small resonator against the faulty channel. You hear two versions of an argument about the roof. Both speakers sound certain. Neither sounds cruel. The resulting roof leaked for seventeen years.

Nacre asks you to help adjust the channel without retuning the whole room. It is a modest task requiring several attempts and one very undignified moment beneath a bucket. The repaired water flow leaves the old argumentative chord intact. They seem happier about the drainage than about any diplomatic success you have witnessed.

On the way out, you ask whether the room's imperfections prove their parent was a poor architect. Nacre looks surprised. "Of course not. They prove my parent built something that had to keep existing after the ceremony." They send a copy of the maintenance instructions to the next apprentice, including the part where both original designers were wrong.

choices.text: Help repair the living room without turning it into a perfect memorial.

effects.journal: Nacre’s family room taught the difference between preserving a record and forcing people to live inside an unchangeable memorial.

scenes.title: A song with an extra verse
paragraphs: Pell's crew are rehearsing a traditional departure song when you arrive. The old verses celebrate speed, courage and a captain who never yielded the sky. The newest verse concerns a civilian freighter that required six tugs and an embarrassing amount of reverse thrust to clear a dock.

The rhyme is poor. The story is true. Pell insisted it remain in the song after a ceremonial officer suggested replacing it with a more dignified victory. "A song which cannot survive a tow cable has an inflated opinion of flight," he says. His junior officers repeat the line later when they believe he cannot hear.

You ask how much of the Yehat's old honor survives the revolution and its aftermath. Pell says more than some reformers expected, less than some admirals prefer. Loyalty, courage and skill are still valuable. The dangerous habit was treating obedience as the thing that made all the others real, and counting a beautiful death more readily than an inconvenient survival.

He shows you a training exercise. The cadet receives three demands: protect the convoy, preserve the fleet and obey a route order. The route is wrong. There is no option that leaves every superior satisfied. The exercise does not award points for disobedience itself. It asks the cadet to record what they knew, whom they consulted and what they were willing to put at risk.

"Several fail by giving magnificent speeches," Pell says. "One passed by calling the tug captain and asking which dock actually had working doors." He turns back to the rehearsal, where the extra verse is finally finding a rhythm. The tug captain has been invited to sing it and is taking entirely too much pleasure in correcting the officers' timing.

choices.text: Stay for the inelegant verse and record the tug captain’s part in the convoy history.

scenes.title: The species in the wrong column
paragraphs: The seedbank's quarantine tray contains a plant labelled INVASIVE, USEFUL, DO NOT COMPOST. Moss asks which part of the label you find contradictory. It grows quickly, stabilizes damaged soil and can destroy native seedlings if introduced without care. Whether it is a rescue or a disaster depends on the place, the quantity and the people maintaining it.

"I am told your species likes stories where a thing's origin settles its moral character," she says. "Gardening is an expensive way to outgrow that habit." She does not mean that all introductions are harmless. The quarantine tray is locked. She means evidence must be more specific than a comforting category.

A former shield world has requested the plant because its roots can bind toxic dust. Another world, with an intact fragile ecology, has refused even a sealed sample. Moss respects both decisions and has prepared different plans. Central dispatch tried to merge the requests under a common recovery protocol. Her reply contains three diagrams and one unusually pointed botanical metaphor.

You ask whether she sees the Afterlight as an introduced species. "I see them as people whose habitat must be designed with care. Calling them natural or unnatural will not tell us the temperature their rooms require." Her own ancestors were once dismissed by another visitor as food that had developed an inconvenient opinion. She remembers this when she is tempted to classify a new life too quickly.

The plant in quarantine pushes a leaf against the glass. Moss trims it gently and records the growth. Compassion has not required her to unlock the tray. Caution has not required her to pretend the plant is malicious. She hopes the final assembly will manage an equally sophisticated relationship with its own vocabulary.

choices.text: Keep the ecological plans specific to each community and its actual conditions.

effects.journal: Moss distinguished origin, risk and moral standing. The harbor needs measured conditions and local control, not a declaration that its inhabitants are natural or unnatural.

scenes.title: The people answering the phones
paragraphs: Sera invites you to observe a dispatch shift before the assembly. The invitation does not include a camera crew. You sit beside an operator who has been awake too long and nevertheless asks a frightened caller to repeat a difficult address without making them feel foolish for needing to do so.

A forecast would once have supplied the missing detail. Now the operator has to call a neighboring station, compare two maps and admit a delay. Another shipment waits while she does. The slower procedure prevents one wrong delivery and postpones one right one. Nobody has found a way to make the trade disappear by giving it a better name.

Sera takes the next call herself. The caller knows who she is and uses the opportunity to complain about three decisions outside her immediate control. She does not explain the organizational chart until the medicine request is settled. Afterwards she tells you that some of her staff oppose the mandate because they want the right to make limited decisions without being treated as embodiments of central authority.

Other staff support it because they know exactly how many broken local systems rely on the office's improvisation. These workers are not a single faction waiting for their leader to be defeated or vindicated. Several will be essential to any future you choose. They deserve a role that is not merely being blamed for the mechanism they kept working during a shortage.

At the end of the shift, the operator from the first call receives an actual arrival confirmation. She smiles for perhaps two seconds, then answers the next line. Sera asks you to remember that smile when designing the replacement. "If the new arrangement cannot do this part," she says, "then our criticism has not yet become a solution."

choices.text: Include dispatch workers as independent participants in the transition plan.

effects.journal: The dispatch shift showed the real work behind central capacity. Any settlement must retain practical expertise without making workers extensions of an unquestionable office.

scenes.title: The price of an ordinary risk
paragraphs: Tallow has an offer from a new insurance consortium. They will reinstate his position if he supplies a risk model for the Afterlight settlements. The model assumes that field-born people are interchangeable when their training records overlap. He has returned it with the polite suggestion that the consortium's directors try sharing one salary whenever they agree about a paragraph.

The reply is sufficiently chilly that he has begun calculating the cost of unemployment. He does not ask you to call his choice brave. "It was an excellent letter. I may have to eat it, but I stand by the punctuation." Anet has offered him a temporary desk at the receiving port. It is close to the arrival doors, which suits his increasingly inconvenient interest in whether people actually appear.

He is redesigning claim categories around failure modes rather than kinds of person. Loss of continuity, denied access, unannounced transfer and absent review each need different protection. The approach makes some premiums harder to estimate. It also catches risks the older forms missed because the claimants were supposed to behave alike.

Lilt asks whether this means the consortium dislikes it. Tallow answers with unusual care. "The consortium dislikes uncertainty that must be priced by people it has not employed. This often looks personal from the receiving end. Sometimes it becomes personal when no one challenges the form."

He gives you a new policy heading: RIGHT TO AN ACTUAL CLAIMANT.
