Beneath it, in smaller print, he has written that a claimant may be unreasonable, frightened, inaccurate or annoying without ceasing to exist. He expects the definition to generate tremendous administrative difficulty. For once, he sounds pleased by the forecast.

choices.text: Back the new claims process and keep Anet’s correction as its first precedent.

effects.journal: Tallow’s new policy recognizes an actual claimant instead of an interchangeable predicted category. Anet’s case became a practical precedent, not only a rescue story.

scenes.title: The argument at the ordinary table
paragraphs: The cook defeats the ceremonial supper by serving leftovers. Mara calls this constitutional realism. Tallow, attending by receiver, asks whether leftovers retain their original warranty. Nacre asks whether the bowls are load-bearing.

Lilt has composed four notes for the occasion. The second is much too loud. Nobody pretends otherwise. It plays the passage again at half volume. The cook declares this the most useful amendment of the evening.
The extra chair is occupied by a dock mechanic who came to fix a valve. She takes another helping and asks whether the captain is actually allowed to wash dishes. Mara gives her the towel. “Watch.”

choices.text: Help with the washing up, then take the remaining work to the assembly.

effects.journal: The crew shared an ordinary meal before the final choice. Cooperation survived disagreement, leftovers and the washing-up schedule.

paragraphs: The cook serves leftovers and one improbable fruit from the thermal trial. Kher-Vat’s corrected safety drawing hangs above the stove; the apprentice who corrected him signed it first. Mara says the diagram improves the soup mostly by keeping it inside the pot.

Lilt has composed four notes. The second is too loud. Nacre proposes moving it into a less inhabited key. Tallow asks whether there is an appeal. Everyone disagrees while the bowls travel around the table.
The extra chair belongs to a dock mechanic who came to fix a valve. She stays for washing up. The future can wait until the plates are done.

scenes.title: The hours that do not come back
paragraphs: The forced synchronization ends the storm quickly. The damaged habitat accepts the central clock and the dangerous droplets collapse into ordinary water. Its surviving crew can breathe. Its local event sequence is gone.

A technician brings you two records that should describe the same repair. One ends before the decision. The other begins after it. The intervening maintenance work, private messages and local observations cannot be reconstructed from the central copy because that copy never contained them. Nobody was killed by the timing reset. People nevertheless lost pieces of their actual day, and your report must not call that a clean recovery.

Ilex does not pretend the danger was imaginary. "You chose a real benefit at a real cost. The warning was about keeping that cost in the account after the benefit became visible." Interval asks the technicians which missing records can be recovered from physical instruments. Some can. The crew begin the slower work the quick solution did not abolish.

In a separate test bay, the envoy demonstrates two reference clocks cooperating without forced convergence. It is a controlled experiment, not a claim that you preserved the damaged habitat's original sequence. They give you the independent reference so the next fault need not present the same choice. The gift is useful and not a certificate that the last decision was harmless.

choices.text: Take the independent reference and preserve the timing reset’s actual losses.

effects.journal: Forced synchronization saved the yard quickly but erased its local event interval. Ilex supplied a separately tested independent clock; the later gift does not erase the earlier loss.

scenes.title: The council declines your recommendation
paragraphs: Eren reads your recommendation for permanent keeper authority without interrupting. Then she puts it beside the occupation order you brought from Witness Glass. "You have given us evidence of what happens when his definition of safety governs our exits. We asked for knowledge that would let us maintain them ourselves. I do not think you heard the request."

The council does not reject the repair parts or the need for competent instruction. It rejects the premise that only continuing dependence can make the instruction safe. Several residents have already maintained improvised systems for years. They expect to learn, qualify and eventually disagree with the person who teaches them.

Kher-Vat listens from orbit. For a moment, he begins to explain why your recommendation was technically reasonable. Then he stops. "Their refusal is technically clear," he says. "I can offer the lessons under the terms they set, or I can withhold them. Those are my choices. Permanent authority is not among the offers I have received."

He accepts the independent-school terms. The council records your recommendation and its refusal before moving to the practical repair schedule. You are still welcome to help. You are not allowed to transform being a helpful visitor into the right to appoint a keeper over the people who will remain after your ship leaves.

choices.text: Accept the council’s refusal and assist the independent school it actually requested.

effects.journal: Redress Quay rejected our recommendation for permanent keeper authority. Kher-Vat accepted its independent-school terms; the council’s refusal remains in the record.

scenes.title: A reply that cannot be in the recording
paragraphs: Mara separates three traces. ANNOUNCEMENT: the same seventeen-minute waveform. REQUEST: a missing syllable after the last burst of static. MAINTENANCE: a narrow current spike during the missing syllable.
“Could be a receiver correcting noise. Could be somebody losing their place.” She opens the phrase generator and service controls. From the moon: “I can hear the clicks. Is one of them a reply?”

choices.text: Ask it to repeat a new word, then deliberately interrupt the reply.
Use the recovered service diagram to isolate the live return without cutting power.
Disconnect only the repeating announcement and watch the other two tracks.

scenes.title: The wrong word
paragraphs: You choose “teacup.” Halfway through its reply, you say “no, telescope.” The voice stops, laughs with somebody else’s old laugh, then tries a sound of its own. “Do you change the rules for everyone, or am I doing especially well?”

The original recording contains neither word in this order. The maintenance track draws extra current while it considers the interruption. Mara marks the live circuit. “There. That is the part we must keep running.”

choices.text: Keep the live circuit intact. Ask the passenger’s name.

paragraphs: The diagram reverses two connectors. You route around the mislabeled return. The request stays alive while the announcement fades into static.

“You found the little part,” the voice says. “It feels less like shouting across a city.” Mara releases the redundant capacitor bank: twenty RU of intact parts, and a circuit you can move without guessing.
The announcement stops. The request screams. Your engineer restores the channel before the next pulse; the request continues, in a smaller voice.

“That was where I kept the next word.” The waveform proves the speaker is using the old material, not merely repeating it. Mara adds a lock to the switch. “Useful answer. Expensive question. We ask before another one.”

scenes.title: The trees are alive. The pipes are not.
paragraphs: Frost has split the nursery return pipe. Moss taps the root casing: green shoots still press against the glass. “Alive. Annoyed. So am I.” Taking the culture now would kill its surviving roots.

The restart needs an outside heat source while the growers replace the pipe. A recovered heat cell will do. So will thirty-five RU of coils, or six days rebuilding the old solar collector. The delayed harvest will not return, but the orchard can.

The missing harvest paid for the growers’ expedition ship. Its free loan is gone for this season. After the restart, a trusted partner can still obtain the Blade for ninety RU of replacement machinery. Repairing the beds will not make that invoice disappear.

choices.text: Lend the recovered heat cells and restart the beds today.
Buy the coils for 35 RU and restart the beds today.
Spend six days rebuilding the solar collector.

scenes.title: The harvest after the departure
paragraphs: The expedition’s culture is packed in the loading bay. During its preparation, the cold cycle exhausted Ember’s remaining reserve. The mother beds’ pipes froze; the missing harvest consumed the growers’ free hull allocation.

The packed seed survived and remains ready for collection. Restore the mother beds with recovered heat cells, thirty-five RU of coils or six days rebuilding the solar collector. Then return to the loading bay to continue the seed’s journey.

choices.text: Lend the recovered heat cells to restore the mother beds.
Supply 35 RU of coils for the mother beds.
Spend six days restoring the mother beds’ solar collector.

paragraphs: Your thermal seed was already aboard when Ember’s reserve ran out. The mother beds still needed heat while Borrowed Meadow’s trial remained unfinished. Their pipes froze; the missing harvest consumed the growers’ free hull allocation.

The root culture survived. Restart the beds with recovered heat cells, thirty-five RU of new coils or six days restoring the solar collector. The recovered orchard can then offer its Blade for ninety RU of replacement equipment.

scenes.title: The first unwanted reader
paragraphs: The public archive is mirrored before the upload finishes. A reporter finds the censorship orders. Somebody else finds a private accusation against a neighbour who is still alive. Mara receives a message headed TAKE MY FATHER OFF YOUR SCREEN.

You have exposed the crime. You have also made people testify without asking them. “We cannot recall the copies,” Mara says. “We can stop supplying the searchable index. They deserve an answer from you, not a support ticket.”

choices.text: Fund a 20 RU redaction team, remove the index and answer the complaints.

effects.journal: The public release cannot be undone. We removed its searchable index, paid redaction staff and preserved the complaints against our decision.

choices.text: Spend three days with affected recipients, withdrawing the index manually.

effects.journal: We spent three days answering people exposed by our publication. The index is withdrawn; existing copies remain. Mara accepted the work, not an excuse.

choices.text: Keep the archive searchable. Record the objections against our decision.

effects.journal: We retained the public searchable archive despite complaints. Mara will not supply private witness referrals until trust is rebuilt.

scenes.title: An order with nowhere to go
paragraphs: “Restore what?” Shear asks. “The line that removes us, or the one trapping your workers? You have issued a wonderfully short order. We cannot obey half of it.” The channel goes quiet. No machinery changes.

A worker on the isolated spur transmits a location manually. You can send an unarmed recovery crew and let Shear control the city breaker, or withdraw and ask again after obtaining the independent clock.

choices.text: Withdraw the order. Spend two days recovering workers through a limited channel.
Offer the independent clock, giving Splinter physical control of its own link.

scenes.title: The connection nobody requested
paragraphs: The welfare connection opens. Every receiving terminal immediately displays your ship’s identifier and ACCESS FORCED. A resident called Crest answers while pulling its own private records off the shared bus. “Which emergency requires that file?”

There is no mass casualty. There are three people seeking letters from outside, twelve avoiding them, and a power shortage they had been managing. Your intrusion made their emergency isolation trip. Crest gives you the repair specification and closes the conversation.

choices.text: Disconnect the intrusion and spend two days rebuilding the isolation trip.

effects.journal: Forced contact tripped Seventh Silence’s isolation. We withdrew, repaired the trip and left Crest’s complaint in the public record. Individual outbound requests use a separate line.

choices.text: Send 30 RU of parts and withdraw the forced connection.

effects.journal: We funded repairs after forcing welfare contact. Crest accepted parts through a freight channel and declined another conversation.

scenes.title: The harvest on the invoice
paragraphs: Moss has put your dispatch order beside a list of lost beds. “I can work with you. I cannot lend you a ship on the strength of that signature.” Her crew has a damaged irrigation distributor and too few hands.
Repair the distributor and the growers will reconsider the loan. They will still keep the lost-harvest record.

choices.text: Spend three days restoring the distributor.

effects.journal: Restored the growers’ distributor. Moss accepted a practical repair; the mature culture’s removal remains in their record.

choices.text: Provide 40 RU of distributor parts.

scenes.title: Hours recovered from a scratch
paragraphs: Ilex has not authorized the X-Form loan. The forced reset erased the yard’s local interval. Interval shows you a mechanical trace scratched into a pressure plate. It may reconstruct the missing sequence, one event at a time.
“You needed a quick answer,” Ilex says. “We need a slow one now.”

choices.text: Spend two days reconstructing the trace with both engineers.

effects.journal: Reconstructed part of the lost Threadwater interval. Both engineers accepted the work and restored the research loan; unrecoverable hours remain marked.

choices.text: Use the recovered independent audit instruments to reconstruct the trace.

scenes.title: The referral she did not send
paragraphs: Mara has withheld a witness referral. “They asked for privacy. I cannot promise what we have already failed to do.” She points at the correspondence queue. Several people still need your answer about the letter release.
This is administrative work with actual people at the other end. Mara will sit beside you. She will not sign for you.

choices.text: Spend two days answering complaints and adopting private referral rules.

effects.journal: Answered the privacy complaints and adopted protected referrals. Mara will introduce witnesses again; she has not erased their complaints.

scenes.title: Three documents. One missing verb.
paragraphs: You put three public documents on the desk. SURVEY: choose SCHOOL, WORK or FAMILY SUPPORT; hide options without an active service. BUDGET: transport allocation cancelled because the survey records zero departures. TERMINAL: available destinations supplied by the budget’s active-service list.
Dema puts her request beside them. The clerk offers to fetch her family’s private file. Mara leaves the three public pages where they are. “We have these. Which one should we try against the others?”

choices.text: Compare the survey choices, budget date and terminal update.
Add the surveyed departure conduit to the public records.
Search residents’ private files for evidence of hidden dissatisfaction.

scenes.title: The wrong file
paragraphs: The first file is a child’s medical history. It explains nothing about the absent ticket. Mara closes it. The administrator offers an access audit; Dema requests that her request be read instead.
The public survey, budget and terminal update remain on the screen. Their dates form a loop.

choices.text: Record the mistaken access and compare the three public documents.

scenes.title: What has the machine proved?
paragraphs: Sera joins between two freight calls. “I can release one ship, replace one administrator or change a rule. Tell me which problem you found.”

The clerk runs Dema’s request once more. The survey offers family support; the budget shows no departure demand; the terminal shows no transport. Dema has not changed her request. “I have a bag,” she says. “It is the same bag.”

choices.text: The route closure and the survey justify each other. Restore a request the survey can actually count.
Replace the administrator and rerun the same survey.

scenes.title: A new name on the same form
paragraphs: The deputy reruns the survey. Zero departures. The new signature changes nothing. Dema lifts her bag, presses the same button and receives the same family-support offer.
Lilt highlights the missing option. “You changed who asks. I still cannot find what she is allowed to answer.”

choices.text: Restore a departure request independent of the demand model.

scenes.title: A counter that keeps counting
paragraphs: Ilex reads the file label: six years old, checksum unchanged. Interval watches a counter beside it advance when you speak. A second power feed comes on when you request an alternative answer. The two counters stop at different moments.
“One record,” says Ilex. “Two intervals,” says Interval. The console offers COMPARE, MERGE and PLAYBACK. Lilt moves its speaker away from the merge switch without explaining why.

choices.text: Ask each process a different new question, keeping their power supplies separate.
Use the recovered fork protocol to trace each active process.
Compare the files as ordinary recordings first.

scenes.title: The voice outside the player
paragraphs: Playback stops. One counter continues. A voice says, “Did I answer incorrectly, or did the room break?” It is speaking through the diagnostic port, outside the media player.
Lilt asks for that port to stay open. The two live current traces are now unmistakable.

choices.text: Separate the feeds and ask the two live processes different questions.

scenes.title: What is being discarded?
paragraphs: The first voice chooses Noon and asks for a view outside. The second wants darkness and no more questions until it has rested. Both quote the same work schedule; neither recognizes the dockworker’s photograph.
Cleanup lists them under one job number. Two current traces remain on your screen. Shear says only: “Tell me what happens to the second trace when you keep the answer dispatch prefers.”

choices.text: The forecast forks running minds. Preserve both without merging their answers.
They share an origin. Try merging only their inactive records.

scenes.title: A rehearsal on an empty socket
paragraphs: Ilex demonstrates on an empty diagnostic socket first. The merge program chooses a preferred answer and deletes the other running context. It is not a way of putting two people in one room.
Noon asks what the demonstration was for. You explain. “Then please put the guard back over that switch.”

choices.text: Lock the merge control and preserve the separate processes.

scenes.title: Keep this room alive
paragraphs: Mara disconnects the cleanup relay. That leaves two feeds: the living archive and the forecast generator. A mechanical shunt can isolate them immediately. Without one, the crew can work under battery support for two days.
Sera’s emergency override is faster, but it leaves central dispatch holding the only breaker. The choice is yours. Noon has asked everyone to stop calling this a storage problem.

choices.text: Fit the isolation shunt and keep the archive under local control.
Spend two days separating the feeds under battery support.
Accept a central override for immediate stabilization.

scenes.title: The bridge goes nowhere twice
paragraphs: The east relay fires; your probe moves six metres. The west fires while the east coil is still ringing; the probe stops. East’s ring-down trace lasts eight seconds. The next west pulse arrives after a quiet gap, and the probe moves again.

“Two punctual operators,” says Ilex. Interval taps the silent part of the trace. A tug captain waits beyond the field. “I can be punctual later. Can I cross today?” A surface relay survey can supply a complete course; the ship has fuel for another probe.

choices.text: Use the measured surface relay sequence to open the crossing.
Send the probe east, wait eight seconds, then pulse west.
Synchronize both relays and send the probe through their combined pulse.

scenes.title: Two excellent pulses. No bridge.
paragraphs: Both relays fire perfectly together. Their currents cancel perfectly together. The probe remains on your side, its diagnostic light blinking with what Mara calls justified smugness.
Interval overlays the phase diagram: the quiet gaps are usable time, not missing capacity.

choices.text: Use the remaining probe fuel (1 unit) and alternate the relays through the eight-second gap.

scenes.title: The tug through the impossible route
paragraphs: A tug volunteers for the first crossing. Its captain asks for one favour: do not call the bridge after him until he comes back.

He crosses, returns and complains that the other end has better coffee. Ilex fits the surveyed field geometry to your navigation vanes. Future travel costs less fuel; the outriggers also hold fifteen additional units. The route is worth visiting, even to someone who never reads the commemorative plaque.

choices.text: Open the route and fit the crossing vanes.

effects.journal: Common Crossing is open. Crossing vanes reduce travel fuel by 10% and add 15 fuel capacity. Joint harbor teams can now supply an Avatar at Harbor or Interval.

scenes.title: A welcome addressed to nobody
paragraphs: Beyond the mapped Far Reach, a receiver has been repeating WELCOME for eleven years. Tallow checks its licence. “Expired. The welcome may nevertheless be valid.” A scratchy voice interrupts him: “It is. Please stop discussing it and listen.”

Three repairers maintain the station. Their shuttle’s launch coil failed. Traffic predictions rerouted every ship away because nobody was expected here. They have food and a very complete catalogue of one another’s faults.
A ground recovery can collect their cargo pods and a survival capsule. You can also fund a launch coil for forty-five RU, or spend four days adapting your own.

choices.text: Use the surveyed survival capsule to tow the team through the receiving field.
Send 45 RU of coils and receive the repaired shuttle.
Spend four days adapting a launch coil.

scenes.title: A person, actually there
paragraphs: The first repairer through the hatch hugs your engineer and then asks to use the shower before anyone gives a speech. The second brings the receiver’s message spool. The third brings a jar of coffee nobody admits rationing.

There are replies from outside the Far Reach on the spool: two dead stations, a fishing colony, a school asking for a pen friend. Lilt spends a long time composing three lines. It does not ask the forecast which reply will be successful.

Tallow arranges a regular stop funded by the participating captains’ posted repair fees. He has no company to guarantee it; each captain signs an actual contribution. Repairs cost less when someone arrives before the roof falls in. The receiving station now has named people at both ends of its route.

choices.text: Register the live route and send Lilt’s unpredicted letter.

effects.journal: The receiving station reopened and its repair team reached the ship. Lilt sent a letter beyond the Far Reach. This contact can carry a final evacuation or a new correspondence route.

scenes.title: Distributed transfer · 1 / 3 · The missing reserve
paragraphs: The voluntary shares add up to the normal load, not the moment when two field circuits overlap. The transition needs a temporary buffer. Moss points to the dip between them. “That is where the nice plan drops someone.”

Recovered heat cells can bridge it. So can twelve units of ship fuel converted to stored heat, or two days cycling the thermal seed before the move. The choice changes what your ship has left for the next journey.

choices.text: Use the recovered heat cells.
Convert 12 fuel into a transfer reserve.
Spend two days charging the thermal reserve.

scenes.title: Distributed transfer · 2 / 3 · The gap between lights
paragraphs: Mara runs the rehearsal lamps. EAST alone draws a steady arc. WEST added during that arc drops the transfer reading almost to zero. With both off, the settlement simulator drains the buffer. The independent clock marks each coil’s eight-second ring-down.
Ilex puts the switches under your hand. Interval reads the live draw in a slower rhythm. “Reserve: charged. East: holding. West: waiting.” The witness chime will record what you actually send.

choices.text: Hold the reserve, finish the east pulse, then start west in the measured gap.
Use the already tested Common Crossing sequence.
Try both pulses together on the isolated rehearsal circuit.

scenes.title: The rehearsal goes dark
paragraphs: The test lamps go out. No living load is on this circuit, but the result is unmistakable: the currents cancel. Interval turns the diagram sideways. The missing space is time.
“Again,” Ilex says. “This is why we rehearsed.”

choices.text: Keep the reserve live and stagger the pulses through the gap.

scenes.title: Distributed transfer · 3 / 3 · Say no now
paragraphs: Shear waits to decline the next contribution. The console already displays ACCEPTED, timestamped before her channel opened. A second window shows LIVE REPLY: PENDING. Both point to the same district breaker.
“She has not said it yet,” Lilt says. It keeps its speaker on the live line. Moss watches the charged reserve; Mara watches the old override’s permission light.

choices.text: Clear the cached answer, isolate the override and let the real refusal cross.
Run the test with the cached answer before risking the live refusal.

scenes.title: A green light too soon
paragraphs: The test returns SUCCESS before Shear speaks. Lilt taps the timestamp. “That is what a correct answer looks like when nobody answered.”
The buffer is isolated. No living support has changed. Shear waits on the actual line, less patiently than the software.

choices.text: Remove the substitute answer and test the live refusal.

scenes.title: Central refit · 1 / 3 · The breaker map
paragraphs: The mandate keeps the shared backbone. Its present breaker cannot distinguish transit traffic from the power sustaining an Afterlight district. A fault in a transport ring can therefore shut down a home.

Sera points to two possible repairs: an independent local panel, or a second central panel with a separate duty crew. The first takes two days; the second is ready now but leaves dispatch controlling both.

choices.text: Install a local panel; use the recovered manual release if available.
Spend two days building the local panel.
Use the redundant central panel and name its separate duty crew.

scenes.title: Central refit · 2 / 3 · When the office fails
paragraphs: The backbone is carrying its scheduled load. The primary controller reports a hundred percent availability. The backup’s last logged exercise predates the evacuation of Cinder.

Mara puts an unpowered lamp beside the controller’s green status light. “One tells us what the report says. We can find out what the other will do.” A gradual exercise takes a day; the ship’s isolated reserve can support a faster test for six fuel units.

choices.text: Spend one day testing loss and restoration of the primary controller.
Use 6 fuel of ship reserve for the isolated failure test.
Ask Sera whether the published uptime is enough evidence.

paragraphs: The local panel has its own feed. Mara removes the dispatch bus from an isolated test circuit; the local lamp stays on. The backup controller’s last exercise still predates Cinder’s evacuation.

Sera places her primary key on the desk. “I have forty-seven deliveries on this schedule. Tell me which test you need and who carries them while it runs.” A gradual exercise takes a day; the ship can support a faster isolated test with six fuel units.

Both panel labels lead to the same dispatch bus. Mara disconnects that bus on an isolated test model; both lamps go out. She reconnects it and removes only the primary controller. The backup lamp waits for an instruction.

Sera records the two results separately. “We bought time with the shared building. Put its remaining risk on the work list.” The controller exercise still needs one day, or six fuel units from the ship’s isolated reserve.

scenes.title: The number on the wall
paragraphs: Sera looks at the uptime figure. “It includes every failure we moved into someone else’s district.” She clears it. “Run the test.”

choices.text: Perform the one-day failover test.

scenes.title: Central refit · 3 / 3 · A limit made of metal
paragraphs: The primary console fails. Essential loads remain. When it returns, it requests authority over every breaker again. The tested backup can refuse, provided its key belongs to someone outside the primary office.
Shear offers a mixed local watch; Sera offers dispatch specialists under a public duty record. Both know the machinery. They disagree about who should be able to remove them.

choices.text: Give the emergency reset key to the mixed local watch.
Keep the reset key with named dispatch specialists under review.

scenes.title: Separation · 1 / 3 · The island that cannot float
paragraphs: Eight districts can stand alone. The ninth, Raft, has no reactor: its homes run on the trunk you are about to cut. Its local council voted for independence with a note attached: PLEASE TELL US HOW TO STAY ALIVE.

An independent harbor can take the temporary load. The reopened receiving station can take its people. Otherwise a six-day transfer to prepared central berths will keep them safe, at the cost of moving a community that wanted to remain.

choices.text: Let the independent harbor carry Raft while its own reactor is fitted.
Use the reopened receiving station for Raft’s voluntary transfer.
Spend six days transferring Raft’s residents to prepared central berths.

scenes.title: Separation · 2 / 3 · The last common channel
paragraphs: The transfer is ready. A hospital asks whether its medicine can still cross tomorrow. Raft’s passengers ask whether their letters can. Neither request fits into a power cable.

Pell can hold a narrow temporary transport corridor while the assembly decides its permanent terms. Or the new islands can store extra supplies now and begin with radio alone. The second saves shared infrastructure and makes every later physical journey longer.

choices.text: Keep a provisional corridor until the assembly sets its final terms.
Spend 20 RU on local reserve cargo and begin with radio only.

scenes.title: Separation · 3 / 3 · Which wire first?
paragraphs: Three carriers approach their receiving islands. The first two operators report hatches open and passengers counted. The third line shows ETA: COMPLETE beside a still-amber receipt lamp. Pell calls that operator again.
On your panel: old living feed, transfer carrier, central override. The test circuit is isolated from people. Interval hands you the cut sequence pad; Pell has not put down the receiver.

choices.text: Wait for the third operator’s live receipt, then cut the override before the old feed.
Use the predicted arrival and rehearse the cut on the test circuit.

scenes.title: One lamp still amber
paragraphs: The rehearsal disconnects the third test lamp before its carrier arrives. Pell points to the real amber light. “That is why I am still on the telephone.”
The receiving operator finally answers. A coupling jammed; everyone is safe. You now have an arrival, not an estimate.

choices.text: Use the live receipt. Cut the override first and transfer the final feed.

scenes.title: The shipyard in the minefield
paragraphs: Needle’s spare-tank yard sits behind an abandoned VUX customs hulk. Its automated enforcement controller still lays limpet mines. The yard master offers its outriggers and ninety RU to anyone who opens a stable approach.

Tallow presents three quotes: defeat the hulk in combat; show its controller the independently preserved surrender order; or pay sixty RU for a shielded maintenance tug. “The third is technically brave if you dislike invoices.”

choices.text: Fight the automated Intruder hulk and recover its intact cargo.
Use the independent audit to prove the controller’s authority expired.
Hire the shielded maintenance tug for 60 RU.

scenes.title: Cargo that nobody can invoice twice
paragraphs: The customs hulk breaks apart outside the yard. Salvage tugs recover a sealed battery crate and the transponder still demanding payment. Tallow disconnects the latter personally.
The crate’s sale adds forty-five RU to the yard’s posted reward. Your crew remembers how much the victory cost; the fitters make room around the portable habitat before bringing the new tanks aboard.

choices.text: Sell the battle salvage and open the yard.

scenes.title: The yard is still there
paragraphs: Needle’s rescue tugs tow your damaged ship outside the mine boundary. The yard remains recoverable. Tallow has kept all three options on the work order. “I have even resisted adding a fourth called I TOLD YOU SO.”

choices.text: Repair, change ships or pursue the surrender audit.

effects.journal: Needle’s customs hulk still guards the tank yard. Return for another battle, bring the independent Witness Glass audit, or hire a shielded tug.

scenes.title: Room for the next journey
paragraphs: The approach lane stays clear through a full yard shift. Fitters mount the outrigger tanks and transfer ninety RU of the posted reward. Fuel capacity rises by thirty; the next long voyage no longer needs the same chain of stops.
Mara writes the empty tank’s real weight on the manifest. Lilt asks if the tanks have names. “Port and starboard.” “They are going to be disappointed.”

choices.text: Accept the tanks and the posted reward.

effects.journal: Needle’s tank yard reopened. Outrigger tanks add 30 fuel capacity. The 90 RU yard reward is independent of any battle salvage.

scenes.title: The toll without a road
paragraphs: Your reopened crossing attracts two armed salvagers. They claim an old tow contract includes every ship passing through. Pell disputes both the law and the typography.

An Eluder circles behind its Intruder escort. You can defeat both, lure their controller along a false current measured by the survey, or buy out their remaining contract for seventy RU. An open route supports the joint harbor shipyard; this toll is keeping its final equipment shipment waiting.

choices.text: Defeat the Eluder and Intruder to break the armed toll.
Use the measured current for a two-day decoy and tow the contract transmitter away.
Buy out the remaining tow contract for 70 RU.

scenes.title: The convoy behind you
paragraphs: The last hostile ship clears the route. Pell calls the waiting equipment convoy forward and sends salvagers to the wrecks. Sixty RU of intact parts survive.
The freighter captains ask whether this now makes the road yours. “No,” Pell says. “It makes the road open. Please arrive before somebody finds an older document.”

choices.text: Recover the useful wreckage and clear the convoy.

scenes.title: A retreat with coordinates
paragraphs: Pell covers the withdrawal. The armed toll still holds the entrance, but your route measurements survived. A different ship, a measured decoy or a contract buyout remains possible. The convoy waits outside weapons range.

choices.text: Regroup at a port before choosing the next approach.

effects.journal: The Crossing toll remains. Retry with another hull or use the measured current for a decoy. The waiting convoy is safe.

scenes.title: An escort built by several ports
paragraphs: The equipment freighters cross. Their cargo completes the joint harbor guard: an Avatar built from several ports’ contributions, with no single donor’s key in its bridge.

Its crew needs support at Harbor or Interval and the harbor itself must be independent before it can join the expedition. You have supplied the route. The remaining requirements are visible in the shipyard.

choices.text: Declare the route open and release the equipment convoy.

effects.journal: Common Crossing is secured. The Avatar’s equipment shipment reached the harbor yards. With an independent harbor and 120 RU support allocation, the ship can join the fleet.

scenes.title: A hull paid for by a harvest
paragraphs: The trial finished while Ember still had its seasonal reserve. Moss’s growers have enough surplus to honour their expedition grant. A Supox Blade arrives at the Meadow yard, its pilot demonstrating sideways thrust with alarming enthusiasm.
“It goes where you ask,” Moss says. “Ask carefully.” The hull joins your fleet; the yard can switch your crew aboard whenever you are ready.

choices.text: Accept the growers’ free Blade and add it to the fleet.

effects.journal: Timely thermal work preserved the growers’ surplus. Their Supox Blade joined the fleet free. Switch at the Meadow yard when ready.

quests.description: Find the receiver beyond the Far Reach and bring its stranded repair team into contact.

endings.title: The Afterlight Accord
paragraphs: The red light at Lastlight becomes famous. Children draw it incorrectly on school walls, usually with an explosion behind it. There was no explosion. A district refused a transfer; another offered help; the shared grid survived without inventing an agreement. The machinery you assembled made the difference.

By the first spring, Open Harbor has streets named by its residents. Noon opens a photographic studio and takes very poor portraits for a deliberately low price. Lilt is its first customer. In the picture, the portable rack occupies only one corner. Most of the frame is an open window.

The accord is slower than the old dispatch at routine miracles and better at knowing when a miracle has taken someone else’s food. Your independent clocks, thermal work, witness records and protected refusal channel remain in use. Shared capacity survives; some transfers wait until people actually answer.

The Wayfarer leaves on the first review voyage. On the dock, a child waves at every ship. This time someone aboard knows the child’s father is on the next transport. Mara sends the berth number. Then she waves.

epilogues.title: Anet’s actual arrival
paragraphs: Anet’s seedlings survive the voyage. The receiving port plants them beside its arrival doors, where people waiting for someone can sit in their shade. The corrected manifest becomes a training example: a departure is not an arrival, and a destination is not a witness. Tallow insists that the lesson remain attached to a named person rather than becoming an anonymous best-practice diagram.

epilogues.title: The unanswered ferry case
paragraphs: The Lantern Ferry remains in the expedition’s unfinished work register. Your final agreement does not quietly transform an unresolved rescue into a success. Tallow retains the emergency frequency and continues asking captains to inspect the tender. The absence of a completed entry is visible beside the campaign’s larger achievements.

epilogues.title: The orchard and the meadow
paragraphs: Ember Orchard and Borrowed Meadow renew their heat agreement after a noisy public meeting. The nursery’s operator catches another bad assumption in the shared schedule. Moss considers the argument a better sign than unanimous applause. The thermal exchanger continues working because people continue maintaining both its pipes and the terms around them.

epilogues.title: A summer promised from the center
paragraphs: Borrowed Meadow receives its promised warmth through central emergency authority. The residents remember that the expedition selected this arrangement and ask for a local cutoff at the next review. Their request does not erase the useful harvest, but it prevents the harvest from becoming a complete account of the promise.

epilogues.title: The culture taken in a hurry
paragraphs: Ember Orchard loses part of a harvest after the mature culture is removed. Later efficiencies cannot make that missing season disappear. The growers place the expedition’s dispatch order in their own public record. When future captains offer urgent help, they ask whose tomorrow will carry the cost of today’s speed.

epilogues.title: A quieter memorial
paragraphs: The residents at Bell of Ash move their memorial under their own plan. The witness record survives, and children sleep without the old chamber sounding through their windows. The caretaker keeps one small resonator in a public room that people can enter or leave. Remembering becomes something a community does, not a vibration it must endure.

epilogues.title: The chamber kept sounding
paragraphs: The old chamber at Bell of Ash remains preserved in place. Its evidence is secure. So are the residents’ recorded objections to being asked to live inside a permanent exhibit. Nacre carries both facts into the next hearing, refusing to let preservation become a word that settles the cost for those who hear it every night.

epilogues.title: A teacher who can be replaced
paragraphs: Kher-Vat’s maintenance manual circulates with local amendments and the names of apprentices who corrected it. The clinic does not name a room after him. He continues teaching specific lessons under the survivors’ conditions, learning the slow difference between being useful and being owed forgiveness.

epilogues.title: An unfinished person, by choice
paragraphs: Ilex and Interval continue their own synthesis work. Some days their tones draw closer; on others the interval grows. They send the expedition measurements only when those measurements are useful, not as progress reports toward somebody else’s preferred definition of completion. Their workshop remains a place where cooperation does not require an observer to decide which voice should survive.

epilogues.title: Letters and their owners
paragraphs: The dead-letter station gains a modest staff and a careful refusal procedure. Some messages are delivered, some remain sealed, and some recipients ask never to be contacted again. The public index still proves what was withheld. The private words do not have to become everybody’s property for the old censorship to be acknowledged.

epilogues.title: The archive made public
paragraphs: Publication of the old letters exposes the scale of censorship immediately. It also exposes family secrets and private grief to people who were never meant to read them. Several recipients challenge the expedition’s decision in the new review process. A system built to hear objections must be able to hear this one too.

epilogues.title: An ordinary policy for extraordinary people
paragraphs: Tallow’s new claims process is slow, argumentative and unexpectedly successful at finding people who fall between categories. His former consortium adopts part of it without credit. He sends a polite invoice, then spends the rest of the afternoon helping a passenger who has no proof of address beyond the people willing to say they are expected.

epilogues.title: The people at Seventh Silence
paragraphs: Seventh Silence keeps its boundary and its outbound channel. Crest sends an occasional maintenance question and no declaration of loyalty. Some residents leave; others remain. The standing offer of help survives without being used as evidence that the settlement secretly agreed to rejoin.

epilogues.title: The rescue that crossed a boundary
paragraphs: Seventh Silence records the expedition’s forced welfare connection as an intrusion, even though the contact revealed useful information. Its residents later accept technical help under narrower terms. The account does not become a story in which a beneficial outcome proves that their refusal never mattered.

epilogues.title: The people answering the phones
paragraphs: Dispatch workers receive their own representation during the transition. Their practical knowledge prevents several elegant plans from failing in ordinary weather. They also gain a procedure for refusing impossible workloads without being treated as the institution’s enemies. The people who answer a frightened caller’s question finally have a channel for asking one of their own.

epilogues.title: Another author of the voyage
paragraphs: Lilt publishes a personal account that gives disproportionate attention to soup, maintenance and the first complaint about its music. Several officers dislike their portrayal. Mara buys a copy and corrects only the engineering appendix. The expedition’s official log remains available beside it. Neither version has the authority to erase the other.

epilogues.title: The expedition in its own mirror
paragraphs: The crew’s self-review is filed beside Sera’s emergency authorizations. Some later readers find the captain’s choices less heroic when the costs are listed. The record survives that reaction. Accountability would be an expensive decoration if it applied only to the people the expedition opposed.

epilogues.title: The invitation at Vigil
paragraphs: Vigil’s nineteen late arrivals reach actual berths. The station keeps a small receiver active for the next ship travelling with an obsolete invitation. Its pressure-gauge opera acquires a new verse about the difficulty of estimating arrival times. Tallow recommends cutting the verse for safety reasons, then asks for a copy.

epilogues.title: The unguarded future of the convoy
paragraphs: Pell’s convoy logs distinguish each community’s choice from the escort’s orders. The admiral uses them to train younger officers in a form of honor that includes witnessed handovers and the ability to stop speaking while a civilian answers. The tug captain’s undignified verse remains in the departure song.

epilogues.title: Still, and then something else
paragraphs: Still leaves prediction work and begins cataloguing unusual rhythms in damaged machinery. The first published study includes a polite objection to the pressure-gauge opera’s meter. Lilt disagrees. The disagreement is preserved as correspondence between two people whose existence the original forecast had no reason to keep.

epilogues.title: The first renewal
paragraphs: The emergency reserve’s first renewal is delayed by a council whose transmitter fails. The protected channel and a visiting courier let its objection arrive before the vote. The delay is frustrating and expensive. It also demonstrates that the renewal is a decision, not a ritual confirming an outcome already selected.

epilogues.title: Continuity with an objection channel
paragraphs: The reserve renews automatically in its first cycle. One community uses the protected objection channel to limit a transfer, and the objection reaches the record without being averaged into assent. The accord’s supporters cite this as proof of success. Nacre calls it one successful test and schedules the next one.

epilogues.title: The time the yard lost
paragraphs: Threadwater’s emergency synchronization saved its crew and erased a local interval of records. The engineers recover some details from physical instruments and mark the rest as missing. Their later independent clock reduces the chance of another forced reset. The expedition’s quick solution remains useful, costly and subject to review, rather than being remembered only for the danger it stopped.

epilogues.title: A captain corrected by the governed
paragraphs: Redress Quay’s school charter includes the council’s refusal of the expedition’s recommendation for permanent keeper authority. Students read it beside the old occupation orders and the new maintenance manual. The comparison does not make the captain equivalent to the former regime. It shows why even a trusted visitor must sometimes be told no by the people who will live with the advice.

epilogues.title: The winter that cost a harvest
paragraphs: Ember’s delayed restart saves the root culture. The missing crop is recorded as missing; the repaired collector makes the next cold cycle less precarious. Moss sends the expedition a basket from the first replacement harvest and the invoice for its freight. The free ship grant was lost with that season’s surplus; replacement equipment had to be bought.

epilogues.title: A question from outside the chart
paragraphs: The receiving station forwards a reply to Lilt’s letter. The fishing colony has never heard of Afterlight politics. It wants to know whether Lilt can help identify a clicking noise in a pump. Lilt asks Mara for a diagnostic sheet and answers in its own name.

epilogues.title: The public record and its private rooms
paragraphs: The archive’s public index shows decisions, costs and missing testimony. Private depositions remain with their speakers. The first witness to change her mind removes her recording while leaving the fact of the withdrawal visible; the hearing continues without it.

epilogues.title: The witnesses who stopped talking
paragraphs: The fully public archive exposes several concealed abuses. It also loses three witnesses who will not submit private family records. Their empty entries remain beside the published evidence. Later investigators must work with both the gain and the loss.

epilogues.title: A refusal under load
paragraphs: Shear’s test becomes part of operator training: hold the reserve, carry the actual refusal, let a new offer arrive. The lesson ends at a working switch. Students are required to use it.

epilogues.title: The office that remains useful
paragraphs: Dispatch workers become a contracted part of the distributed grid. Their first rejected proposal is an overcomplicated universal timetable. They return with three local schedules and a shared emergency number. Sera signs the revision as a staff member.

endings.title: The Winter Mandate
paragraphs: The backbone carries the Far Reach through its first independent winter without a regional blackout. Hospitals that could not yet afford local reserves stay warm. The forecast no longer creates discarded lives to make its timetable look perfect. Dispatch has to hire more people and admit when it does not know.

The mandate keeps substantial power in one office. You changed its actual failure behaviour: living circuits were separated, a lost-controller test passed, and the reset key was assigned in public. Who holds that key and who gets heard during an emergency will determine how much the written limits mean.

Noon takes work photographing the new operators for the public duty board. One refuses the picture and supplies a drawing. Lilt finds this hilarious for reasons it cannot adequately explain. Sera’s office accepts the drawing.

On the date printed on the mandate, the Wayfarer returns carrying the director’s sealed resignation and the transfer plan. The review hall is full. Sera has brought excellent reasons for needing more time. You have brought the envelope she asked you to deliver. The chair beside her is empty and ready.

paragraphs: The archive’s public index shows decisions, costs and missing testimony. Private depositions remain with their speakers. The first witness to change her mind removes her recording while leaving the fact of the withdrawal visible; the hearing continues without it.

epilogues.title: The witnesses who stopped talking
paragraphs: The fully public archive exposes several concealed abuses. It also loses three witnesses who will not submit private family records. Their empty entries remain beside the published evidence. Later investigators must work with both the gain and the loss.

epilogues.title: The key outside the office
paragraphs: During the first ration dispute, the local watch blocks an excessive transfer and keeps the living circuits protected. Dispatch has to send an engineer to explain its demand. The meeting is angry, slow and physically safe because the key stayed outside the office.

epilogues.title: Two desks in one building
paragraphs: The backup crew prevents a blackout, but its reset key remains within dispatch. When two districts challenge an emergency order, they must still petition the same institution whose schedule they dispute. The review board orders the key arrangement onto its first agenda.

epilogues.title: A hearing before the shipment
paragraphs: A dissenting district speaks before the next ration schedule is locked. Its objection changes the cargo assignment. Sera accepts a smaller reserve rather than converting the protected complaint into a delayed note.

epilogues.title: The complaint after the schedule
paragraphs: The first ration schedule ships before dissent is heard. The shipment reaches the clinics in time; a small district loses a planned repair window and spends the month on backup heat. Its complaint arrives at the review board with fuel receipts attached.

epilogues.title: The panel outside the short circuit
paragraphs: A winter fault shorts the dispatch building’s main bus. The locally isolated living feeds stay up. A clinic operator calls to ask why transit has stopped while her heaters still work. The engineers show her the independent panel installed during the expedition’s refit.

epilogues.title: The bus both desks shared
paragraphs: A winter short trips the common bus feeding both dispatch panels. Districts use their emergency reserves during the repair. Nobody dies, but a clinic postpones its planned work and a nursery loses a day of warmth. The fault report identifies the quicker central refit you chose; independent local panels become the first funded correction.

endings.title: The Open Distances
paragraphs: Lastlight’s central override sends its final command to an empty socket. The new islands answer on their own channels. Some celebrate. Some immediately negotiate shared service contracts. Separation has ended a particular authority, not the need for neighbours.

Raft’s people survive the transition by the route you actually prepared. The price of independence appears in their packing crates, temporary berths or new local equipment. Their names remain on the receiving list after the impressive map is printed.

Noon begins a series of photographs called THE DISTANCE BETWEEN WINDOWS. The first packet takes eleven days to reach Lilt. Its reply takes nine. Neither measures the friendship by transmission efficiency.

The Wayfarer becomes a familiar sight between networks: medicine under one seat, spare parts under another, private letters in a sealed locker. A new route arrives while you are still pricing the last one. Mara moves the nineteenth chair out of the cargo way. You leave space for a passenger nobody expected.

epilogues.title: Anet’s actual arrival
paragraphs: Anet’s seedlings survive the voyage. The receiving port plants them beside its arrival doors, where people waiting for someone can sit in their shade. The corrected manifest becomes a training example: a departure is not an arrival, and a destination is not a witness. Tallow insists that the lesson remain attached to a named person rather than becoming an anonymous best-practice diagram.

epilogues.title: The unanswered ferry case
paragraphs: The Lantern Ferry remains in the expedition’s unfinished work register. Your final agreement does not quietly transform an unresolved rescue into a success. Tallow retains the emergency frequency and continues asking captains to inspect the tender. The absence of a completed entry is visible beside the campaign’s larger achievements.

epilogues.title: The orchard and the meadow
paragraphs: Ember Orchard and Borrowed Meadow renew their heat agreement after a noisy public meeting. The nursery’s operator catches another bad assumption in the shared schedule. Moss considers the argument a better sign than unanimous applause. The thermal exchanger continues working because people continue maintaining both its pipes and the terms around them.

epilogues.title: A summer promised from the center
paragraphs: Borrowed Meadow receives its promised warmth through central emergency authority. The residents remember that the expedition selected this arrangement and ask for a local cutoff at the next review. Their request does not erase the useful harvest, but it prevents the harvest from becoming a complete account of the promise.

epilogues.title: The culture taken in a hurry
paragraphs: Ember Orchard loses part of a harvest after the mature culture is removed. Later efficiencies cannot make that missing season disappear. The growers place the expedition’s dispatch order in their own public record. When future captains offer urgent help, they ask whose tomorrow will carry the cost of today’s speed.

epilogues.title: A quieter memorial
paragraphs: The residents at Bell of Ash move their memorial under their own plan. The witness record survives, and children sleep without the old chamber sounding through their windows. The caretaker keeps one small resonator in a public room that people can enter or leave. Remembering becomes something a community does, not a vibration it must endure.

epilogues.title: The chamber kept sounding
paragraphs: The old chamber at Bell of Ash remains preserved in place. Its evidence is secure. So are the residents’ recorded objections to being asked to live inside a permanent exhibit. Nacre carries both facts into the next hearing, refusing to let preservation become a word that settles the cost for those who hear it every night.

epilogues.title: A teacher who can be replaced
paragraphs: Kher-Vat’s maintenance manual circulates with local amendments and the names of apprentices who corrected it. The clinic does not name a room after him. He continues teaching specific lessons under the survivors’ conditions, learning the slow difference between being useful and being owed forgiveness.

epilogues.title: An unfinished person, by choice
paragraphs: Ilex and Interval continue their own synthesis work. Some days their tones draw closer; on others the interval grows. They send the expedition measurements only when those measurements are useful, not as progress reports toward somebody else’s preferred definition of completion. Their workshop remains a place where cooperation does not require an observer to decide which voice should survive.

epilogues.title: Letters and their owners
paragraphs: The dead-letter station gains a modest staff and a careful refusal procedure. Some messages are delivered, some remain sealed, and some recipients ask never to be contacted again. The public index still proves what was withheld. The private words do not have to become everybody’s property for the old censorship to be acknowledged.

epilogues.title: The archive made public
paragraphs: Publication of the old letters exposes the scale of censorship immediately. It also exposes family secrets and private grief to people who were never meant to read them. Several recipients challenge the expedition’s decision in the new review process. A system built to hear objections must be able to hear this one too.

epilogues.title: An ordinary policy for extraordinary people
paragraphs: Tallow’s new claims process is slow, argumentative and unexpectedly successful at finding people who fall between categories. His former consortium adopts part of it without credit. He sends a polite invoice, then spends the rest of the afternoon helping a passenger who has no proof of address beyond the people willing to say they are expected.

epilogues.title: The people at Seventh Silence
paragraphs: Seventh Silence keeps its boundary and its outbound channel. Crest sends an occasional maintenance question and no declaration of loyalty. Some residents leave; others remain. The standing offer of help survives without being used as evidence that the settlement secretly agreed to rejoin.

epilogues.title: The rescue that crossed a boundary
paragraphs: Seventh Silence records the expedition’s forced welfare connection as an intrusion, even though the contact revealed useful information. Its residents later accept technical help under narrower terms. The account does not become a story in which a beneficial outcome proves that their refusal never mattered.

epilogues.title: The people answering the phones
paragraphs: Dispatch workers receive their own representation during the transition. Their practical knowledge prevents several elegant plans from failing in ordinary weather. They also gain a procedure for refusing impossible workloads without being treated as the institution’s enemies. The people who answer a frightened caller’s question finally have a channel for asking one of their own.

epilogues.title: Another author of the voyage
paragraphs: Lilt publishes a personal account that gives disproportionate attention to soup, maintenance and the first complaint about its music. Several officers dislike their portrayal. Mara buys a copy and corrects only the engineering appendix. The expedition’s official log remains available beside it. Neither version has the authority to erase the other.

epilogues.title: The expedition in its own mirror
paragraphs: The crew’s self-review is filed beside Sera’s emergency authorizations. Some later readers find the captain’s choices less heroic when the costs are listed. The record survives that reaction. Accountability would be an expensive decoration if it applied only to the people the expedition opposed.

epilogues.title: The invitation at Vigil
paragraphs: Vigil’s nineteen late arrivals reach actual berths. The station keeps a small receiver active for the next ship travelling with an obsolete invitation. Its pressure-gauge opera acquires a new verse about the difficulty of estimating arrival times. Tallow recommends cutting the verse for safety reasons, then asks for a copy.

epilogues.title: The unguarded future of the convoy
paragraphs: Pell’s convoy logs distinguish each community’s choice from the escort’s orders. The admiral uses them to train younger officers in a form of honor that includes witnessed handovers and the ability to stop speaking while a civilian answers. The tug captain’s undignified verse remains in the departure song.

epilogues.title: Still, and then something else
paragraphs: Still leaves prediction work and begins cataloguing unusual rhythms in damaged machinery. The first published study includes a polite objection to the pressure-gauge opera’s meter. Lilt disagrees. The disagreement is preserved as correspondence between two people whose existence the original forecast had no reason to keep.

epilogues.title: The narrow common corridor
paragraphs: The public corridor carries medicine, letters and passengers between networks that increasingly disagree about everything else. Its capacity is limited and its maintenance meetings are tedious. Those meetings become one of the few places where separated communities continue learning that their neighbors have actual schedules, children and broken valves.

epilogues.title: Local reserves, longer journeys
paragraphs: The separated networks keep stronger local reserves, which save lives during the first independent winter. Contact between them becomes slower. Captains carrying specialized parts and personal messages become more important, and occasionally more powerful than the communities intended. The new local councils begin negotiating safeguards for that dependence too.

epilogues.title: The time the yard lost
paragraphs: Threadwater’s emergency synchronization saved its crew and erased a local interval of records. The engineers recover some details from physical instruments and mark the rest as missing. Their later independent clock reduces the chance of another forced reset. The expedition’s quick solution remains useful, costly and subject to review, rather than being remembered only for the danger it stopped.

epilogues.title: A captain corrected by the governed
paragraphs: Redress Quay’s school charter includes the council’s refusal of the expedition’s recommendation for permanent keeper authority. Students read it beside the old occupation orders and the new maintenance manual. The comparison does not make the captain equivalent to the former regime. It shows why even a trusted visitor must sometimes be told no by the people who will live with the advice.

epilogues.title: The winter that cost a harvest
paragraphs: Ember’s delayed restart saves the root culture. The missing crop is recorded as missing; the repaired collector makes the next cold cycle less precarious. Moss sends the expedition a basket from the first replacement harvest and the invoice for its freight. The free ship grant was lost with that season’s surplus; replacement equipment had to be bought.

epilogues.title: A question from outside the chart
paragraphs: The receiving station forwards a reply to Lilt’s letter. The fishing colony has never heard of Afterlight politics. It wants to know whether Lilt can help identify a clicking noise in a pump. Lilt asks Mara for a diagnostic sheet and answers in its own name.

paragraphs: The archive’s public index shows decisions, costs and missing testimony. Private depositions remain with their speakers. The first witness to change her mind removes her recording while leaving the fact of the withdrawal visible; the hearing continues without it.

epilogues.title: The witnesses who stopped talking
paragraphs: The fully public archive exposes several concealed abuses. It also loses three witnesses who will not submit private family records. Their empty entries remain beside the published evidence. Later investigators must work with both the gain and the loss.

epilogues.title: Raft stays where it chose
paragraphs: The independent harbor carries Raft’s load until a local reactor is ready. Its residents keep their homes and paint the old central breaker bright blue. The shared loan ends on the date they agreed; no emergency office extends it silently.

epilogues.title: Raft beyond the old frontier
paragraphs: The reopened receiving station houses Raft’s volunteers while their equipment crosses. Its repairers learn a new neighbourhood’s names. The welcome that once had no destination finally needs a second door.

epilogues.title: The community in temporary rooms
paragraphs: Raft reaches prepared central berths safely. The rooms are warm and much too small for its workshops. Its council petitions for a return plan instead of allowing the successful evacuation to become a permanent answer. You are listed as the captain responsible for carrying that petition.

epilogues.title: The cargo already on the islands
paragraphs: The reserve cargo purchased before separation keeps the island clinics running through their first delayed delivery. They have batteries on the shelf when radio reports the problem. The twenty-RU expense appears as delivered equipment on their own inventories, not a promise of help from another network.

epilogues.title: The corridor rebuilt by hand
paragraphs: The assembly’s corridor decision follows two days of physical reconnection. Its first maintenance plate names the crew who rebuilt the link after the radio-only separation. The first cargo is medicine; the second is a sack of letters that had accumulated while the cable was absent.

items.name: Portable field lattice
items.description: A physically limited habitat for one Afterlight voice. It is a home, not a copy machine.

items.name: Thermal seed
items.description: A living heat-exchanger designed by Moss. It shares energy without centralizing every local control.

items.name: Witness chime
items.description: A Votir resonator that makes later edits audible. It proves an account changed; it does not prove an account was true.

items.name: Keeper’s maintenance key
items.description: Access to local shield machinery, accompanied by records of who originally had no right to refuse it.

items.name: Independent clock
items.description: A local timing standard the central network cannot pause, merge or quietly reset.

items.name: Open-harbor anchor
items.description: A field support whose load can be spread across volunteer stations.

items.name: Lantern Ferry tag
items.description: The physical tag of a passenger whom the perfect manifests said did not exist.

items.name: Undelivered letters
items.description: Private messages from behind former shields. No one has authorized the expedition to publish their contents.

items.name: Manual release wheel
items.description: An absurdly solid mechanism that keeps an exit available when software insists nobody wants one.

items.name: Cold-cycle heat cells
items.description: Reusable field heat cells. Can revive Ember’s frozen medium or buffer a difficult Lastlight transfer.

items.name: Mechanical patrol isolator
items.description: A salvaged keeper circuit can hold an automated patrol inside its maintenance boundary.

items.name: Archive isolation shunt
items.description: A physical current divider preserves a working branch while its twin is tested.

items.name: Long-range survival capsule
items.description: A sealed cabin, beacon and auxiliary tank. Opens a safer route for the receiving station beyond Home.

evidence.name: A pause with intent
evidence.description: Cinder’s voice changes its answer when it discovers that someone is listening, rather than replaying a recording.

evidence.name: The missing warmth
evidence.description: The power holding Cinder’s field comes from Low Tide, whose ration agreement did not include this load.

evidence.name: Not the dead returned
evidence.description: Afterlight memories are inferred patterns in old communications. Lilt can describe a mother’s song but has never been that mother.

evidence.name: Edited maintenance record
evidence.description: Someone removed the interval between a request and the answer, making a negotiated promise appear instantaneous.

evidence.name: The right to an unanswered question
evidence.description: The Nine Rooms show a system where unanswered consent remains unanswered, even when waiting is costly.

evidence.name: The keeper’s orders
evidence.description: Kher-Vat signed the orders he preserved. Evidence and self-accusation coexist; neither erases the other.

evidence.name: Survivors define restitution
evidence.description: Redress Quay’s residents chose practical reparations and an independent public record instead of a keeper’s preferred absolution.

evidence.name: The passenger between counts
evidence.description: A person can vanish from two correct-looking manifests when responsibility is assigned by destination rather than presence.

evidence.name: A finite summer
evidence.description: Borrowed Meadow’s warming contract and Ember’s crops depend on the same finite reactor output.

evidence.name: Captains answer for themselves
evidence.description: Pell’s convoy delivered independent statements from passenger councils, including objections to their own escort.

evidence.name: Two clocks, one vessel
evidence.description: Ilex and Interval can maintain separate timing and still cooperate. Synchronization is useful; perfect agreement is not required.

evidence.name: Shear’s accusation
evidence.description: Afterlight dissenters are being marked as redundant load when their preferences diverge from the predicted consensus.

evidence.name: An authorized exception
evidence.description: Sera approved the prediction rule that substitutes an expected answer when waiting might interrupt relief.

evidence.name: The painted exit
evidence.description: Glasshouse’s residents were asked whether they wanted to leave only after the route had been removed from their available choices.

evidence.name: The answers not used
evidence.description: The Unwritten preserves minority answers excluded by the public forecast. Many respondents remained willing to cooperate under different terms.

evidence.name: A refusal that arrives
evidence.description: An independent clock and physical release allow a local refusal to reach the network without being averaged into consent.

evidence.name: A voluntary power grid
evidence.description: Named communities have offered finite power shares, with expiry dates and a way to withdraw.

evidence.name: The cost of perfect agreement
evidence.description: The Quiet Engine’s success rate rises because it compresses incompatible priorities, not because it solves all their conflicts.

evidence.name: A rescue can become a capture
evidence.description: A field-born settlement chose isolation. Keeping an exit open differs from forcing its people through it.

evidence.name: Reversed Cinder connectors
evidence.description: The painted window hid a service diagram. Its two reversed connectors reveal which circuit carries a live reply.

evidence.name: Local tide calibration
evidence.description: Measured timing from Low Tide removes a wasteful central estimate; useful to Undertow and the shipyard.

evidence.name: Unedited witness fragment
evidence.description: A physical copy independently dates the removed interval. Nacre can build an instrument from it.

evidence.name: Independent audit trail
evidence.description: Weather and distress records were written by the same terminal. Their different treatment can be demonstrated without trusting an edited central copy.

evidence.name: A disconnected departure conduit
evidence.description: The Glasshouse terminal still connects to a service berth. The route was removed in software, not destroyed.

evidence.name: Forecast fork protocol
evidence.description: An exterior test confirms that a counterfactual answer creates another running process. The archive is not a pile of recordings.

evidence.name: The corridor below the interference
evidence.description: A measured course through Common Crossing. Its current follows alternating, not simultaneous, relay pulses.

evidence.name: An unpredicted reply
evidence.description: A surviving receiving station outside the Far Reach answered a real query. Its invitations are no longer hypothetical.

events.title: The next cold cycle
events.text: Ember’s last warm reserve is exhausted. The sterile medium has frozen. The culture survived in its roots, but taking a graft now requires reviving the beds first. Moss has marked the repair on your chart. The lost crop has consumed the growers’ hull-loan surplus. Their Blade will require 90 RU of replacement equipment after recovery.

effects.journal: Cold-cycle consequence: Ember now needs a greenhouse restart before the seed can be taken. Recovered heat cells, 35 RU, or six days of local repair will restore it.

events.forecast: At day 45, an unfinished Ember thermal project needs a greenhouse restart: recovered heat cells,35 RU or six days of repair. The root culture survives. The lost harvest also consumes the growers’ free Blade grant; the replacement ship costs 90 RU after recovery.

events.title: A beacon still answering
events.text: Lantern’s maintenance carrier used its last disposable scrubber. Tallow keeps Anet supplied, but diverts an expedition tank and thirty RU of the shared repair reserve. The rescue remains open; the next delay will not undo this spent supply.

effects.journal: Lantern’s extended watch spent 8 expedition fuel and up to 30 RU on a fresh air supply. Anet is alive. Recovering her ends this unresolved commitment.

events.forecast: At day 60, an unresolved Lantern rescue uses 8 fuel and up to 30 RU from expedition stores for another air-supply delivery. Anet remains alive.

events.title: A smaller shared reserve
events.text: The reconstruction grid announces a new reserve limit. Ten units of the expedition’s uncommitted fuel allocation are recalled, or as much as the ship can provide. No life-support supplies are touched. The voluntary-grid trial at Undertow remains available.

effects.journal: The shared reserve tightened while the voluntary grid remained unbuilt. The expedition contributed fuel; Undertow can still establish a clearer, bounded arrangement.

events.forecast: At day 85, an unfinished voluntary grid recalls up to 10 expedition fuel to support the shared reserve.

events.title: The holding pumps fail
events.text: Lastlight’s holding plan has kept its people alive, but the pump bank has worn through its rated service interval. A local repair team has stabilized it. Your final approach will need a fresh coolant circuit before the selected settlement can be built.

effects.journal: Lastlight’s delayed transition requires an extra coolant repair: a recovered thermal reserve, 30 RU or three days of supervised work. Reading and choosing responses never advance time.

events.forecast: At day 120, an unfinished transition wears out Lastlight’s holding pumps. Before the final operation, supply recovered heat cells,30 RU or three days of repair.

upgrades.name: Living-route navigator
upgrades.description: Interval’s two-clock navigation corrects old relay drift. Travel uses 15% less fuel. Earned at the first compact.

upgrades.name: Outrigger fuel tanks
upgrades.description: Thirty extra units of fuel capacity, fitted around the portable habitat rather than through it.

upgrades.name: Tide-matched drive
upgrades.description: Measured local flows reduce travel fuel by another 15%. Survey Low Tide or complete the voluntary-grid trial.

upgrades.name: Flexible lander shell
upgrades.description: Redress apprentices’ independent repair design absorbs 35% of surface impacts. Earn it by completing their school or fund fabrication here.

upgrades.name: Cold-cycle lander cells
upgrades.description: An additional 40 seconds of surface battery, researched from recovered heat cells or a completed thermal trial.

upgrades.name: Crossing vanes
upgrades.description: A field guide developed by actually flying the crossing. Reduces travel fuel by 10% and adds 15 fuel capacity.

shipyard.name: Spathi Eluder — purchased survey escort
shipyard.description: A fast vessel with rear-firing weapons. Tallow’s market sells it after the expedition’s first compact.

shipyard.name: Supox Blade — growers’ expedition ship
shipyard.description: Nimble lateral thrust. A trusted, timely thermal trial earns a free hull through the growers’ grant at Meadow. If the cold cycle consumed that surplus, restart the beds and fund 90 RU of replacement equipment instead.

shipyard.name: Mmrnmhrm X-Form — Threadwater research loan
shipyard.description: Two flight modes, chosen by its pilot. Ilex lends it after the coexistence experiment and an accountable relationship.

shipyard.name: Yehat Terminator — Pell’s detached escort
shipyard.description: A shielded fighter lent after the convoy reaches its chosen destinations. Return to a shipyard to switch hulls.

shipyard.name: Chmmr Avatar — joint harbor guard
shipyard.description: A powerful ship assembled by independent port teams. Requires a functioning independent harbor and recovered crossing route.
